If one understands the differences between these three types of karma, one gains correct view, as stated in the verse: “Those who commit evil and see happiness have not yet ripened their evil karma; when their evil karma ripens, they will see suffering. Those who commit good and see suffering have not yet ripened their good karma; when their good karma ripens, they will see happiness.”

Furthermore, the Discrimination of Great Karma Sutra states: “Those who do not kill will be reborn in heaven, provided they had merit in a previous life or developed a strong virtuous mind at the moment of death.” Those who understand this cause right view. Therefore, one should understand the characteristics of these three kinds of karma.
content.pt:
Pergunta: O Buddha disse no sutra que há três tipos de karma: karma imediato, karma futuro e karma subsequente. O que são eles?

Resposta: Se alguém cria karma nesta vida, recebe os resultados nesta vida; isto é chamado de retribuição imediata. Se alguém cria karma nesta vida e recebe os resultados na próxima vida, isto é chamado de retribuição na próxima vida. Se alguém cria karma nesta vida e recebe os resultados após a próxima vida, isto é chamado de retribuição na vida subsequente, porque ocorre após a próxima vida.

Pergunta: Onde o karma do estado intermediário é recebido?

Resposta: É recebido em dois lugares. O karma intermediário é recebido no lugar de retribuição futura, porque há uma diferença de nascimento, portanto, é chamado de intermediário. O restante do karma intermediário é recebido no lugar da retribuição tardia.

Pergunta: Estes três tipos de karma são determinados por retribuição ou pelo mundo?

Resposta: Alguns dizem que a retribuição é determinada, o que significa que o karma imediato deve ser recebido na vida presente, e o mesmo se aplica aos outros dois. Embora isso seja dito, o significado não está correto. Por que é assim? Se assim fosse, não apenas as cinco ofensas graves seriam chamadas de retribuição fixa, mas o Abhidharma também diz que as cinco ofensas graves são de retribuição fixa.

Além disso, o Sutra do Sal também diz que não é fixa, e que existem ações kármicas que deveriam resultar em retribuição infernal, mas devido ao cultivo de moralidade, preceitos, mente e discernimento pela pessoa, elas são capazes de receber a retribuição nesta vida. Portanto, esses três tipos de karma devem ser mundanos. O karma presente não resulta necessariamente em retribuição imediata; se resultar, deveria ser recebido nesta vida e não noutro lugar. O mesmo se aplica aos outros dois.

Pergunta: Que tipo de karma pode receber retribuição imediata?

Resposta: Alguns dizem que o karma motivado por ganho ou ódio recebe retribuição imediata, assim como o bom ou mau karma em relação ao Buddha, aos nobres ou aos próprios pais. Esta é a retribuição imediata. Se o karma é nocivo e pesado, é retribuição na próxima vida. Por exemplo, as cinco ofensas graves são tanto prejudiciais como pesadas, por isso recebem retribuição na próxima vida, assim como o karma de um rei girador da roda ou o karma de um bodhisattva. Outros dizem que estes três tipos de karma recebem retribuição de acordo com os desejos da pessoa. Se a intenção é que o karma seja recebido nesta vida, é uma retribuição imediata. Por exemplo, a Senhora Mallika deu sua própria porção de alimento ao Buddha e desejou tornar-se rainha nesta vida. Os outros dois tipos de karma são semelhantes.

Além disso, a retribuição é recebida conforme o amadurecimento do karma.

Pergunta: O que se entende por amadurecimento do karma passado?

Resposta: Quando os aspectos pesados estão totalmente presentes, chama-se amadurecimento.

Pergunta: Existe algo como o karma surgindo de um único pensamento e a retribuição sendo recebida no pensamento seguinte?

Resposta: Não, a retribuição é recebida gradualmente. Isso é semelhante a como uma semente gradualmente brota. A lei do karma é a mesma.

Pergunta: Pode-se acumular karma enquanto no útero ou num estado de sono ou loucura?

Resposta: Aqueles que possuem pensamentos podem acumular karma, mas ele não está totalmente desenvolvido.

Pergunta: Se alguém deixar este lugar, pode ainda realizar o karma deste lugar?

Resposta: Aqueles com senso do eu podem acumular este karma, mas se alguém abandonar o senso de eu, não mais o acumula.

Pergunta: Por que os Arhats, que também prestam homenagens e cultivam méritos, não acumulam tal karma?

Resposta: Porque todos os seres têm a mente do eu, o karma acumula-se. Os Arhats não têm a mente do eu, portanto o karma não se acumula.

Além disso, a mente dos Arhats está livre de impurezas, e uma mente livre de impurezas não acumula karma. Os sutras também dizem que aquele que cortou tanto as ofensas kármicas como os méritos é chamado um Arhat. Tal pessoa não acumula ofensas kármicas, mérito, ou karma imóvel. Portanto, uma vez que o seu karma se esgota, eles não criam um novo karma.

Pergunta: Aqueles que estão aprendendo acumulam karma?

Resposta: Eles também não o acumulam.

Por que isso? O sutra diz: "Esta pessoa dispersa e destrói todos os karmas; não os acumula, não os reúne, e não os extingue." Alguns estudiosos dizem que aqueles que estão aprendendo possuem orgulho, de modo que seu karma também se acumula, mas devido a seu discernimento do não-eu, eles não recebem necessariamente suas consequências.

Pergunta: Em qual reino podem esses três tipos de karma ser criados?

Resposta: Podem ser criados em todos os lugares dentro dos três reinos.

Pergunta: Os karmas indeterminados são existentes ou inexistentes?

Resposta: São existentes. Se o karma resulta em retribuição imediata, futura ou tardia, ele é chamado indeterminado. Tal karma é abundante.

Pergunta: Qual benefício se ganha ao compreender estes três tipos de karma?

Resposta: Se se pode distinguir esses três tipos de karma, causa-se o surgimento da visão correta. Por que assim? Vê-se que os que cometem ações ruins desfrutam de riqueza e prazer, enquanto os que fazem boas ações sofrem. Entre eles, alguns podem causar visões erradas, pensando que o bem e o mal não têm retribuição. Se se entende as diferenças entre os três tipos de karma, ganha-se a visão correta, como está no verso: "Aqueles que cometem o mal e veem a felicidade ainda não amadureceram seu mau karma; quando ele amadurecer, eles verão o sofrimento. Aqueles que cometem o bem e veem sofrimento ainda não amadureceram seu bom karma; quando ele amadurecer, verão a felicidade."

Além disso, o Sutra da Discriminação do Grande Karma afirma: "Aqueles que não matarem renascerão no céu, se tiverem tido mérito numa vida anterior ou tiverem desenvolvido uma mente virtuosa forte no momento da morte." Aqueles que compreendem isso causam a visão reta. Portanto, deve-se entender as características dos três tipos de karma.

segments.label: 105 三受報業品 (On the Threefold Karma Receiving Retribution | Retribuição)

content.zh:
問曰：經中佛說三種業，樂報、苦報、不苦不樂報業。何者是耶？
答曰：善業得樂報，不善業得苦報，不動業得不苦不樂報，此業不
必定受，若受則受樂報，非苦等；餘二亦爾。
問曰：是諸業亦得色報，何故但說受耶？

答曰：於諸報中受為最
勝，受是實報，色等為具。又於緣中說受，如說火苦火樂。或有因
中說果，如人施食名施五利，亦如言食錢等。
問曰：從欲界至三禪中，得受不苦不樂報耶？

答曰：得受。
問曰：是何業報？

答曰：是下善業報，上善業則受樂報。
問曰：若爾，何故第四禪及無色定中說耶？

答曰：彼是自地。所以
者何？彼中但有是報更無異受，以寂滅故。
問曰：有人言，憂非業報。是事云何？

答曰：何故無耶？
問曰：憂但從想分別生，業報不應是想分別故。又若憂是業報，業
報則輕，故非報也。又此憂離欲時斷，業報不爾，離欲時不斷，是
故憂非業報。

答曰：汝言憂從想分別生故非報者，樂亦是業報，是
樂二種，一樂、二喜。喜亦從想分別生，不應名報。汝言業報則
輕，是憂重過於苦。

所以者何？憂是愚人，所有智者則無，是故難
除，亦能深生熱惱。又四百觀中說：小人身苦，君子心憂。又此憂
要以智斷，身苦樂亦能除。又憂能生三世中惱，所謂我先有苦、今
苦、當苦。又憂是諸煩惱住處，如經中為煩惱處故說十八意行，以
五識中不生煩惱故。又經中說以憂為二箭，以受苦重故。如人一處
重被二箭，則受苦倍增。如是癡人為苦所逼，更增憂患以惱身心，
故甚於苦也。又愚者常憂。

所以者何？是人恩愛乖離、怨憎合會、
所求不得等故常憂惱。又此憂從二因生，一從喜生、二從憂生。若
失所愛物是從喜生，如經中說，佛問波斯匿王：汝愛迦尸憍薩羅國
耶？

又說：諸天樂色貪色，是色若壞則生憂惱。是名從喜生。從憂
生者，從所憎事生，亦從嫉妬等生。未離欲者嫉妬等結常惱其心，
如說天人多慳嫉結。又多眾生憂惱他人，故得憂惱報，如說隨種生
果。故知憂是業報。汝言離欲時斷故非報者，是事不然，須陀洹未
離欲亦斷地獄等報，可以地獄等報為非報耶？故不可以離欲時斷便
名非報。
問曰：不苦不樂報業名不動，此業是善應受樂報，何故受不苦不樂
報耶？

答曰：是受不動故實樂，以寂滅故名不苦不樂。又經中說樂
受中貪使，彼中貪於彼受中使，故知是樂。
content.en:
The Buddha said in the sutra that there are three kinds of karma: karma with pleasant retribution, karma with painful retribution, and karma with neither pleasant nor painful retribution. What are these?

Answer: Good karma leads to pleasant retribution, evil karma leads to painful retribution, and neutral karma leads to neither pleasant nor painful retribution. These karmas are not necessarily received; if received, they are pleasant retribution, not painful, etc. The same applies to the other two.

Question: These karmas also produce material retribution; why is only “retribution” mentioned?

Answer: Among all retributions, “retribution” is the most excellent; “retribution” is the true retribution, while material forms are merely accessories. Additionally, ‘retribution’ is discussed in terms of conditions, such as saying “fire is painful” or “fire is pleasant.” Sometimes the result is mentioned in the cause, such as when a person gives food and it is called “giving the five benefits,” or when one speaks of “eating money.”

Question: From the desire's realm to the third dhyana, do beings receive neither pleasant nor unpleasant retributions?

Answer: They do receive retributions.

Question: What kind of karma is this?

Answer: It is the retribution of lower virtuous karma. Higher virtuous karma results in pleasant retributions.

Question: If that is the case, why is it mentioned in the fourth dhyana and the formless realms?

Answer: Because they are their own realms. Why? Because in those realms there is only this retribution and no other sensations, due to stillness and extinction.

Question: Some say that sorrow is not a karmic retribution. How is this?

Answer: Why not?

Question: Sorrow arises from conceptual discrimination, and karmic retribution should not be conceptual discrimination.

Furthermore, if sorrow is a karmic retribution, then karmic retribution would be light, and thus not a retribution.

Furthermore, sorrow ceases when desire is eliminated, but karmic retribution does not cease when desire is eliminated. Therefore, sorrow is not karmic retribution.

Answer: You say that sorrow arises from conceptual discrimination and therefore is not retribution. But pleasure is also karmic retribution. There are two kinds of pleasure: one is pleasure, and the other is joy. Joy also arises from conceptual discrimination and should not be called retribution. You say that karmic retribution is light, but sorrow is heavier than suffering. Why is that? Sorrow is the domain of the ignorant; the wise do not have it, so it is difficult to eliminate and can deeply stir up distress.

Furthermore, the Four Hundred Verses state: “The small person suffers physically, while the noble person suffers mentally.”

Moreover, this sorrow must be severed by discernment. Physical suffering can be eliminated by pleasure. Additionally, sorrow can cause distress in the three realms, namely, past suffering, present suffering, and future suffering.

Furthermore, worry is the dwelling place of all afflictions. As the sutra says, the eighteen mental activities are called the dwelling places of afflictions because afflictions do not arise from the five senses. The sutra also says that worry is like two arrows because suffering is heavy. Just as a person struck by two arrows in one place suffers twice as much, so too, deluded people, being tormented by suffering, increase their worries and afflictions, tormenting their minds and bodies, and thus suffer even more than suffering itself.

Furthermore, the foolish are always anxious.

Why is this? Because they are separated from those they love, reunited with those they hate, and unable to obtain what they desire, they are constantly anxious and distressed.

Moreover, this anxiety arises from two causes: one from joy, and the second from anxiety. If one loses what one loves, this arises from joy. As the sutra says, the Buddha asked King Prasenajit, “Do you love the kingdom of Kasi?” It is also said, "The gods delight in form and are greedy for form. When form is destroyed, they experience sorrow and distress. This is called arising from joy. Arising from sorrow, it arises from things one hates, and also from jealousy and the like. Those who have not abandoned desire are constantly tormented by jealousy and the like, as it is said that heavenly beings have many jealous knots.

Furthermore, many beings cause sorrow to others and thus receive the fruit of sorrow. As it is said, “The fruit ripens according to the seed.” Therefore, we know that sorrow is the result of karma. You say that since it ceases when desire is abandoned, it is not a result. This is not the case. The Stream-Enterer, though not yet free from desire, has already cut off the retributions of hell and other realms. Can we say that the retributions of hell and other realms are not results? Therefore, we cannot say that because it ceases when desire is abandoned, it is not a result.

Question: The karma that is neither pleasant nor unpleasant is called immovable. This karma is good and should bring pleasant karma, so why does it bring neither pleasant nor unpleasant karma?

Answer: It is truly pleasant because it is immovable, and it is called neither pleasant nor unpleasant because it is still.

Furthermore, the sutra says that greed arises in the realm of pleasure, and that greed in that realm acts as a driving force. Therefore, we know that it is a pleasure.
content.pt:
O Buddha disse no sutra que existem três tipos de karma: karma com retribuição agradável, karma com retribuição dolorosa, e karma com retribuição nem agradável nem dolorosa. Quais são eles?

Resposta: O bom karma leva à retribuição agradável, o mau karma leva à retribuição dolorosa, e o karma neutro leva à retribuição nem agradável nem dolorosa. Esses karmas não são necessariamente recebidos; se recebidos, são retribuição agradável, não dolorosa, etc. O mesmo se aplica aos outros dois.

Pergunta: Esses karmas também produzem retribuição material; por que apenas a "retribuição" é mencionada?

Resposta: Entre todas as retribuições, a "retribuição" é a mais excelente; a "retribuição" é a verdadeira retribuição, enquanto as formas materiais são meramente acessórios. Adicionalmente, a 'retribuição' é discutida em termos de condições, como dizer "o fogo é doloroso" ou "o fogo é agradável". Às vezes o resultado é mencionado na causa, como quando uma pessoa dá comida e isso é chamado de "dar os cinco benefícios", ou quando se fala de "comer dinheiro".

Pergunta: Do reino do desejo até o terceiro dhyana, os seres recebem retribuições nem agradáveis nem desagradáveis?

Resposta: Eles de fato recebem retribuições.

Pergunta: Que tipo de karma é este?

Resposta: É a retribuição de um karma virtuoso inferior. O karma virtuoso superior resulta em retribuições agradáveis.

Pergunta: Se esse for o caso, por que é mencionado no quarto dhyana e nos reinos sem forma?

Resposta: Porque eles são seus próprios reinos. Por quê? Porque nesses reinos só há esta retribuição e nenhuma outra sensação, devido à quietude e à extinção.

Pergunta: Alguns dizem que a tristeza não é uma retribuição kármica. Como é isso?

Resposta: Por que não?

Pergunta: A tristeza surge da discriminação conceitual, e a retribuição kármica não deveria ser discriminação conceitual.

Além disso, se a tristeza for uma retribuição kármica, então a retribuição kármica seria leve e, assim, não seria uma retribuição.

Além disso, a tristeza cessa quando o desejo é eliminado, mas a retribuição kármica não cessa quando o desejo é eliminado. Portanto, a tristeza não é retribuição kármica.

Resposta: Você diz que a tristeza surge da discriminação conceitual e, portanto, não é retribuição. Mas o prazer também é retribuição kármica. Existem dois tipos de prazer: um é o prazer e o outro é a alegria. A alegria também surge da discriminação conceitual e não deveria ser chamada de retribuição. Você diz que a retribuição kármica é leve, mas a tristeza é mais pesada do que o sofrimento. Por que é assim? A tristeza é o domínio dos ignorantes; os sábios não a têm, de modo que é difícil de eliminar e pode suscitar profundamente o sofrimento.

Além disso, os Quatrocentos Versos afirmam: "A pessoa pequena sofre fisicamente, enquanto a pessoa nobre sofre mentalmente."

Além disso, esta tristeza deve ser cortada pelo discernimento. O sofrimento físico pode ser eliminado pelo prazer. Adicionalmente, a tristeza pode causar sofrimento nos três reinos, isto é, sofrimento passado, sofrimento presente e sofrimento futuro.

Além disso, a preocupação é a morada de todas as aflições.

Como diz o sutra, as dezoito atividades mentais são chamadas de moradas das aflições porque as aflições não surgem dos cinco sentidos. O sutra também diz que a preocupação é como duas flechas porque o sofrimento é pesado. Assim como uma pessoa atingida por duas flechas no mesmo lugar sofre o dobro, também as pessoas iludidas, sendo atormentadas pelo sofrimento, aumentam as suas preocupações e aflições, atormentando as suas mentes e corpos, e assim sofrem ainda mais do que o sofrimento em si.

Além disso, os tolos estão sempre ansiosos.

Por que isso é assim? Porque estão separados daqueles a quem amam, reunidos com aqueles a quem odeiam, e incapazes de obter o que desejam, eles estão constantemente ansiosos e angustiados.

Além disso, esta ansiedade surge de duas causas: uma da alegria, e a segunda da ansiedade. Se alguém perde o que ama, isso surge da alegria. Como o sutra diz, o Buddha perguntou ao Rei Prasenajit: "Você ama o reino de Kasi?" Também é dito: "Os deuses se deleitam na forma e são cobiçosos por ela. Quando a forma é destruída, eles experimentam tristeza e angústia. Isto é chamado de surgir da alegria. Surgindo da tristeza, surge das coisas que se odeia e também do ciúme e coisas assim. Aqueles que não abandonaram o desejo são constantemente atormentados pelo ciúme e por sentimentos semelhantes, pois se diz que os seres celestiais têm muitos nós de ciúmes.

Além disso, muitos seres causam tristeza aos outros e assim recebem o fruto da tristeza. Como é dito: "O fruto amadurece de acordo com a semente". Portanto, sabemos que a tristeza é o resultado do karma. Você diz que, como cessa quando o desejo é abandonado, não é um resultado. Esse não é o caso. Aquele que Entrou na Correnteza, embora ainda não livre do desejo, já cortou as retribuições do inferno e de outros reinos. Podemos dizer que as retribuições do inferno e de outros reinos não são resultados? Portanto, não podemos dizer que, porque cessa quando o desejo é abandonado, não é um resultado.

Pergunta: O karma que não é agradável nem desagradável é chamado de imóvel. Este karma é bom e deveria trazer karma agradável, então por que ele não traz um karma nem agradável nem desagradável?

Resposta: É verdadeiramente agradável porque é imóvel, e é chamado de nem agradável nem desagradável porque é quieto.

Além disso, o sutra diz que a ganância surge no reino do prazer e que a ganância nesse reino atua como força motriz. Portanto, nós sabemos que é um prazer.

segments.label: 106 三障品 (On the Three Obstacles | Sobre On the Three Obstacles)

content.zh:
問曰：經中說三障，業障、煩惱障、報障。何者是耶？

答曰：若諸
業煩惱及報，能障解脫道，故名曰障。
問曰：何者能障？

答曰：施戒修善回向三有，此能障道。又定受報
業是亦為障，

如經中說：若此人必定集受報業，則不入正位。是名
業障。又若人煩惱厚利增上常在心中，是煩惱障。又若人煩惱不可
除遣，如不能男等欲，亦名煩惱障。又若地獄等罪惡生處，及隨所
生處不能修道，皆名報障。
問曰：有人不先明悉前人，不知其善則不布施，謂彼人若由我施得
造諸惡，我則有分，如梵志等諸出家人，故出家人不應布施，以新
業繫障解脫故。

答曰：不然。他作罪福於我無分。

所以者何？罪福
因緣中有多過咎。何者？如眾生是殺因緣，若無眾生何所殺耶？然
則死者應當有罪。又如富者是盜因緣，美色是邪婬因緣，他人是妄
語等因緣，偽稱等是欺誑因緣，買者亦應有罪。又受者為施者因
緣，亦應得福。若人造井池等用者皆應得福，然則不應自為福德，
而實不然，是故因緣中不應有罪福。又受者福分應當消盡，則人不
應從他受施。

所以者何？以福德分貿飲食故。又施者應罪多而福
少。

所以者何？詎有幾所婆羅門能為善者？多以三毒濁心深著五欲
不勤修善，是故施者應罪多福少。又梵志等自稱善人修行法者，是
人不能正觀諸法禪定攝心，若離禪定心難調伏，是故施者施未離欲
人應得罪多。又人供養父母、供給妻子親屬知識皆應得罪，則無有
人得福分者，而實不然，是故罪福不在因緣中。又持戒等法亦利益
他，是人不殺生故施一切命，則持戒者得大罪分，以不殺故前人得
壽。所作眾惡盡，應是持戒者分，故求福者便當殺生不應持戒。又
人說法令他修福，修福因緣後得富貴，富貴則憍逸，憍逸則造諸
惡，此諸惡說法者皆應有分。又施因緣令他人富，以富因緣所作諸
罪，亦應是施者分。然則梵志不應受施亦不應與，而今梵志但受不
與，故知此為邪道。又如諸王如法治民亦應有罪。又若子為罪而父
母有分，則應不生子。又良醫療疾亦應得罪，以其得命為諸罪故。
又天降時雨生長五穀，天應得罪，以多濟育惡眾生故。又施食者亦
應得罪，受者或食不消乃令至死，亦未離欲人以著味故施者應罪。
然則施者常應令受者自立誓言：今食汝食要不為惡，然後當與。若
不如是，則施者兩失。
問曰：經中亦言，若比丘食檀越食、著檀越衣入無量定，以是因緣
故此檀越得無量福。若以是因緣而得福者，云何不得罪耶？

答曰：
若是比丘食檀越食、著檀越衣入無量定，檀越施福自得增長，不得
定福。如田良故所收必多，薄則收少。如是福田良故施報則大，薄
則福少，不以受者為福為罪而施者得分，是故不以罪福因緣而得罪
福。彼雖為因緣，而罪福要由自起三業。
問曰：未離欲人心不自在必貪著有，故出家人不應行施。

答曰：若
爾，則出家人持戒等皆有福德，是亦應捨，而實不可，是故布施亦
不應捨，但勿回向三有，當為泥洹。又但應遠離煩惱諸不善業。所
以者何？是諸業，因時可防、果時無可如何。是故諸佛常於因時教
化說法，不如閻王於果時方化訶責。
問曰：是三業障中何障最重？

答曰：有人言，報障最重，以不可化
故。有人言，以隨人故一切皆重。
問曰：何者可轉？

答曰：皆可令滅，若可轉者不名為障也。
content.en:
The sutra speaks of the three obstacles: the obstacle of karma, the obstacle of afflictions, and the obstacle of retribution. What are these?

Answer: If karma, afflictions, and retribution obstruct the path to liberation, they are called obstacles.

Question: What obstructs?

Answer: Giving, precepts, cultivating virtue, and directing merit toward the three realms—these obstruct the path.

Furthermore, samskaras and karma that are destined to be reborn are also obstacles. As the sutra says, “If this person is destined to receive karma, he will not enter the correct path.” This is called karma obstacle.

Furthermore, if a person's afflictions are thick and powerful, always present in the mind, this is called affliction obstacle.

Furthermore, if a person's afflictions cannot be eradicated, like the desires of an impotent man, this is also called affliction obstacle.

Furthermore, if one is born in hell or other evil realms, or if one cannot cultivate the path wherever one is born, these are all called karmic obstacles.

Question: Some people do not first clearly understand others, and if they do not know their good deeds, they do not make offerings, thinking that if those people commit evil deeds because of their offerings, they will share in the blame, like Brahmins and other monks. Therefore, monks should not make offerings, as new karma binds and obstructs liberation.

Answer: This is not the case. The sins and merits of others have no share in me.

Why is this? Because in the causal conditions of sins and merits, there are many faults and shortcomings. What are they? For example, sentient beings are the causal condition for killing. If there were no sentient beings, what would be killed? Then the killer should be guilty. Again, wealth is the causal condition for theft, beauty is the causal condition for adultery, others are the causal condition for false speech, and deceitful claims are the causal condition for fraud. Then the buyer should also be guilty.

Furthermore, the recipient is the cause of the giver, and should therefore receive merit. If those who use wells and ponds should all receive merit, then one should not create merit for oneself, which is not the case. Therefore, there should be no merit or demerit in the causes and conditions.

Furthermore, the recipient's merit should be exhausted, so one should not receive offerings from others.

Why is this? Because merit is exchanged for food and drink.

Furthermore, the giver should have more demerit than merit. Why is this so? How many Brahmins are truly capable of doing good? Most are deeply attached to the three poisons of greed, hatred, and ignorance, indulging in the five desires, and neglecting the cultivation of virtue. Therefore, the giver should have more sin and less merit.

Furthermore, those who claim to be virtuous and practice the Dharma, such as Brahmins, are unable to correctly observe the nature of all dharma or cultivate samadhi to concentrate the mind. If they depart from samadhi, their minds become difficult to tame. Therefore, when the giver makes offerings to those who have not yet abandoned desire, they should incur more sin.

Furthermore, if one offers support to one’s parents, provides for one’s spouse and relatives, and supplies one’s friends, one should incur guilt, and thus no one would receive merit. But this is not the case. Therefore, guilt and merit do not depend on causes and conditions.

Moreover, observing precepts and other practices also benefit others. Those who do not kill living beings offer life to all beings. Thus, those who observe precepts incur great guilt, for by not killing, they enable others to live longer. All the evil deeds they have committed should be their share. Therefore, those seeking merit should kill living beings and not observe precepts.

Furthermore, some teach others to cultivate merit through the law, claiming that cultivating merit will lead to wealth and honor, which in turn lead to arrogance and the commission of various evils. Thus, those who teach this doctrine should share in the evil consequences of these actions. Similarly, if one gives to others to make them wealthy, the sins committed by those who become wealthy should also be the giver’s share. However, Brahmins should neither accept nor give alms. Yet today, Brahmins only accept and do not give, so we know this is a wrong path. Similarly, kings who govern their people according to the law should also be guilty.

Furthermore, if a child commits a crime, should the father and mother also share in the guilt? If so, one should not have children.

Moreover, good doctors who cure diseases should also be guilty, as they preserve life, which is a sin.

Furthermore, when heaven sends timely rain to nourish the five grains, heaven should be guilty, as it nourishes many evil beings. Similarly, those who give food should be guilty, as the recipient may not digest it and die, or those who have not yet abandoned desire may become attached to the taste, thus making the giver guilty. Therefore, the giver should always make the recipient swear: “I will not commit evil after eating your food,” and then give it. If not, both the giver and the recipient lose.

Question: The sutra also states that if a monk eats the food of a layperson, wears the clothes of a layperson, and enters a state of deep meditation, the layperson will gain immeasurable merit because of this cause and effect. If one gains merit because of this cause and effect, how can one not incur sin?

Answer: If a monk eats the food of a layperson, wears the clothes of a layperson, and enters a state of deep meditation, the layperson’s merit increases, but the monk does not gain the merit of deep meditation. Just as a fertile field yields a bountiful harvest, while a barren field yields little, so too, when the field of merit is fertile, the reward for giving is great; when it is barren, the merit is small. The giver does not gain merit or incur guilt based on the recipient’s condition, but rather the giver alone reaps the benefits. Therefore, merit and guilt are not determined by the cause and effect of giving or receiving. Though the cause and effect exist, merit and guilt ultimately arise from one’s own three karmas.

Question: Since those who have not abandoned desire are not free from greed and attachment to existence, monks should not practice giving.

Answer: If that were the case, then monks who keep the precepts would all have merit, and they should also abandon it. But this is not possible, so giving should not be abandoned. However, one should not direct the merit toward the three realms of existence but toward Nirvana.

Furthermore, one should distance oneself from all unwholesome actions. Why? Because these actions can be prevented at the time they arise but cannot be altered once their results have manifested. Therefore, the Buddhas always teach and expound the Dharma during the time of cause, rather than waiting until the time of result to admonish and rebuke like Yama.

Question: Among the three karmic obstacles, which is the heaviest?

Answer: Some say that the retributive obstacle is the heaviest, because it cannot be transformed. Others say that since it follows the person, all are heavy.

Question: Which can be transformed?

Answer: All can be extinguished. If it can be transformed, it is not called an obstacle.

segments.label: 107 四業品 (On the Fourfold Karma | Karma)

content.zh:
問曰：經中佛說四種業，黑黑報業、白白報業、黑白黑白報業、不
黑不白無報業。為滅盡諸業故，何者是耶？

答曰：黑黑報業者，隨
以何業生苦惱處，如阿鼻地獄及餘苦惱無善報處，若畜生、餓鬼少
分。與此相違名第二業，隨以何業生無苦惱處，如色無色界及欲界
人天少分。黑白雜名第三業，隨以何業生苦惱不苦惱處，若地獄、
畜生、餓鬼、人天少分。第四業名無漏，能盡三業。若業二世所
呵，今呵、後呵，是人為罪墮在黑闇。無有名聞故名為黑。及二世
苦毒，今苦、後苦，故名為黑。
問曰：是業何者能生純苦惱處？

答曰：相次為惡心無有悔，間無有
善能消惡業，是名能生純苦惱處。又以邪見心而造諸惡。又於重人
為惡，所謂父母及餘善人。又於眾生為惡無所遺惜，如殺眾生若盡
奪財物、若閉牢獄而復斷食、若重考掠令無餘樂，如是等業生純苦
處。白白報業者，若人純集諸善、無有不善，此二業勢力最大，餘
無能勝。若受黑業報時不容白報，受白業報時不容黑報。所以者
何？一切眾生皆集善不善，業力相障故不得並受。如負二人物，強
者先牽。第三業弱，善不善雜故，並受報互相勝故。
問曰：有人言，若不善業受惡道報是名初業，色界繫善名第二業，
欲界繫天人中雜受報業是名第三業，無礙道中十七學思是第四業。
此義云何？

答曰：佛自說此業等相，謂若人起罪身口意行，受苦惱
身生苦惱處，所受諸受皆不隨意。故知隨令眾生生純苦處，是名初
業。色無色界則純受樂，欲界天人亦有純受樂者，

如經說：有樂人
亦有六觸入，天所覺諸塵無不隨意，是第二業。黑白雜行是第三
業。一切無漏業皆是盡諸業，以相違故，非但十七學思，名第四
業。
問曰：無漏實白，何故名不白耶？

答曰：此白相異，不同第二業
白，是白最勝無相待故。如說轉輪聖王成就清淨過人天眼，實是人
眼勝餘人，故名曰過人。此業亦爾，勝餘白業，故說不白。又有人
言，應說名非黑白報業。此則無過。又泥洹名非白，是故此業應名
非白。又亦應說非黑非白。

所以者何？泥洹名無法，此業為泥洹，
故名不黑不白。又世間貴重有漏善業故名為白，以第四業能捨此業
故名不白。又此業無黑相故，亦無白相可得。又報白故業名白，是
業無報故不名白。
content.en:
In the sutras, the Buddha spoke of four types of karma: black-black karma, white-white karma, black-white-black karma, and neither black nor white karma with no retribution. To eliminate all karma, which of these is it?

Answer: Black-black karma refers to karma that leads to suffering in realms such as Avici hell and other realms of suffering with no good retribution, such as the animal realm and the hungry ghost realm to a lesser extent. The opposite of this is called the second type of karma, which leads to rebirth in places free from suffering, such as the form and formless realms, and to a lesser extent, the human and heavenly realms. The third type of karma is called mixed karma, which leads to rebirth in places where there is both suffering and no suffering, such as hell, the animal realm, the hungry ghost realm, and to a lesser extent, the human and heavenly realms. The fourth type of karma is called pure karma, which can eliminate the three types of karma. If karma is condemned in two lifetimes, condemned now and condemned later, this person is guilty and falls into darkness. It is called darkness because there is no fame. And because there is suffering in both lifetimes, suffering now and suffering later, it is called darkness.

Question: What kind of karma can produce a place of pure suffering?

Answer: Successively committing evil deeds without regret, and in between not having any good deeds to offset the evil karma, this is called karma that produces a place of pure suffering.

Furthermore, with wrong views, one commits various evil deeds. One also commits evil deeds against important people, such as one's parents and other good people. One also commits evil deeds against all beings without mercy, such as killing beings, completely taking their possessions, imprisoning them and depriving them of food, or torturing them severely until they have no joy left. Such deeds cause pure suffering realms. Those who receive white retribution are those who have accumulated only good karma and no evil karma. The power of these two types of karma is the greatest, and nothing can overcome them. When receiving black karma, white karma cannot be received; when receiving white karma, black karma cannot be received.

Why is this? All sentient beings accumulate both good and evil karma, and the forces of karma obstruct one another, so they cannot be received simultaneously. It is like carrying two people on one's back; the stronger one is pulled first. The third type of karma is weak, as it is a mixture of good and evil, and when the two types of karma are received together, they overcome each other.

Question: Some say that if evil karma is repaid in the evil realms, this is called the first type of karma; good karma bound to the form realm is called the second type of karma; karma bound to the desire's realm, which is repaid in the heavens and among humans, is called the third type of karma; and the seventeen types of learning and thinking in the path of no obstacles is called the fourth type of karma. What is the meaning of this?

Answer: The Buddha himself explained the characteristics of these karmas. If a person commits evil deeds with body, speech, or mind, they will be reborn in a realm of suffering and experience suffering. All the sensations they experience are not under their control. Therefore, causing beings to be reborn in a realm of pure suffering is called the first karma. In the form and formless realms, beings purely experience pleasure. In the desire's realm, there are also beings who purely experience pleasure, as the sutra says: “There are beings who experience pleasure, yet they also have the six sense organs. The dusts perceived by the gods are all in accordance with their will.” This is the second karma. The mixed actions of black and white are the third karma. All defilement-free karma are the karma that exhaust all karma, as they are contrary to defilement. Therefore, it is not merely the seventeen types of learning and reflection that are called the fourth karma.

Question: “Defilement-free karma are inherently pure; why are they called ‘not pure’?”

Answer: This whiteness is different from the whiteness of the second karma. It is the highest whiteness without any contrast. For example, the wheel-turning sage king has attained pure eyes that surpass those of humans and gods. These eyes are truly superior to those of ordinary people, hence they are called “superior.” This karma is the same; it surpasses other white karmas, hence it is called “not white.” Some say it should be called “non-black-and-white retributive karma.” This is also acceptable.

Furthermore, Nirvana is called “non-white,” so this karma should be called “non-white.” It should also be called “neither black nor white.” Why? Because Nirvana is called “without dharma,” and this karma leads to Nirvana, so it is called “neither black nor white.”

Moreover, worldly precious karma is called ‘white’ because it is a defiled good karma. Since the fourth karma abandons this karma, it is called “non-white.”

Furthermore, this karma has no black aspect, so there is no white aspect to be found.

Furthermore, because it is white, the karma is called white; since this karma has no retribution, it is not called white.
content.pt:
In the sutras, the Buda spoke of four types of karma: black-black karma, white-white karma, black-white-black karma, and neither black nor white karma with no retribution. To eliminate all karma, which of these is it?

Answer: Black-black karma refers to karma that leads to sofrimento (duḥkha) in realms such as Avici hell and other realms of sofrimento (duḥkha) with no good retribution, such as the animal realm and the hungry ghost realm to a lesser extent. The opposite of this is called the second type of karma, which leads to rebirth in places free from sofrimento (duḥkha), such as the form and formless realms, and to a lesser extent, the human and heavenly realms. The third type of karma is called mixed karma, which leads to rebirth in places where there is both sofrimento (duḥkha) and no sofrimento (duḥkha), such as hell, the animal realm, the hungry ghost realm, and to a lesser extent, the human and heavenly realms. The fourth type of karma is called pure karma, which can eliminate the three types of karma. If karma is condemned in two lifetimes, condemned now and condemned later, this person is guilty and falls into darkness. It is called darkness because there is no fame. And because there is sofrimento (duḥkha) in both lifetimes, sofrimento (duḥkha) now and sofrimento (duḥkha) later, it is called darkness.

Question: What kind of karma can produce a place of pure sofrimento (duḥkha)?

Answer: Successively committing evil deeds without regret, and in between not having any good deeds to offset the evil karma, this is called karma that produces a place of pure sofrimento (duḥkha).

Furthermore, with wrong views, one commits various evil deeds. One also commits evil deeds against important people, such as one's parents and other good people. One also commits evil deeds against all beings without mercy, such as killing beings, completely taking their possessions, imprisoning them and depriving them of food, or torturing them severely until they have no joy left. Such deeds cause pure sofrimento (duḥkha) realms. Those who receive white retribution are those who have accumulated only good karma and no evil karma. The power of these two types of karma is the greatest, and nothing can overcome them. When receiving black karma, white karma cannot be received; when receiving white karma, black karma cannot be received.

Why is this? All sentient beings accumulate both good and evil karma, and the forces of karma obstruct one another, so they cannot be received simultaneously. It is like carrying two people on one's back; the stronger one is pulled first. The third type of karma is weak, as it is a mixture of good and evil, and when the two types of karma are received together, they overcome each other.

Question: Some say that if evil karma is repaid in the evil realms, this is called the first type of karma; good karma bound to the form realm is called the second type of karma; karma bound to the desire's realm, which is repaid in the heavens and among humans, is called the third type of karma; and the seventeen types of learning and thinking in the path of no obstacles is called the fourth type of karma. What is the meaning of this?

Answer: The Buda himself explained the characteristics of these karmas. If a person commits evil deeds with corpo, speech, or mente, they will be reborn in a realm of sofrimento (duḥkha) and experience sofrimento (duḥkha). In the form and formless realms, beings purely experience prazer. In the desire's realm, there are also beings who purely experience prazer, as the sutra says: “There are beings who experience prazer, yet they also have the six sense organs. The dusts perceived by the gods are all in accordance with their will.” This is the second karma. The mixed actions of black and white are the third karma. All defilement-free karma are the karma that exhaust all karma, as they are contrary to defilement. Therefore, it is not merely the seventeen types of learning and reflection that are called the fourth karma.

Question: “Defilement-free karma are inherently pure; why are they called ‘not pure’?”

Answer: This whiteness is different from the whiteness of the second karma. It is the highest whiteness without any contrast. For example, the wheel-turning sage king has attained pure eyes that surpass those of humans and gods. These eyes are truly superior to those of ordinary people, hence they are called “superior.” This karma is the same; it surpasses other white karmas, hence it is called “not white.” Some say it should be called “non-black-and-white retributive karma.” This is also acceptable.

Furthermore, Nirvana is called “non-white,” so this karma should be called “non-white.” It should also be called “neither black nor white.” Why? Because Nirvana is called “without dharma,” and this karma leads to Nirvana, so it is called “neither black nor white.”

Moreover, worldly precious karma is called ‘white’ because it is a defiled good karma. Since the fourth karma abandons this karma, it is called “non-white.”

segments.label: 108 五逆品 (On the Five Heinous Crimes | Sobre On the Five Heinous Crimes)

content.zh:
次身受報故名無間，若現受則輕、苦惱報少，以其重故，次第疾墮
阿鼻地獄。三逆由福田德重故名為逆，所謂破僧、惡心出佛身血、
殺阿羅漢；殺父母，以不識恩養故名為逆。此逆罪但人道中能起，
非餘道中，以人有別知故。
問曰：殺餘聖人得逆罪不？

答曰：殺聖人者多墮地獄，若殺阿羅漢
必應當墮。若人打佛而血不出，亦得重罪，以欲害世尊故。
問曰：若人作一逆罪則墮地獄，若作二三亦於一身盡受報不？答
曰：是罪多故，又受重苦，於是中死還生是中。
問曰：破僧罪中云何為重？

答曰：若非法知非法、是法知是法，如
是心作則名為重。若非法謂法、法謂非法，是不如先。又若人於佛
所破僧，自稱大師、天人中尊，是亦為重。
問曰：若凡夫可破非是聖人，何名重罪？

答曰：障礙正法故名重
罪。
問曰：破僧法為幾時？

答曰：法不久住，不經一宿。是中梵王等諸
天、舍利弗等諸大弟子即還和合。有人言，是五百比丘先世障他得
道善根因緣，今得此報。又凡夫人心輕躁故易可破壞，若但得世間
空無我心尚不可壞，況無漏耶。以惡欲在心故造破僧因緣，故求福
者應捨惡欲。◎
◎
content.en:
The Five Grave Offenses receives retribution, hence it is called “uninterrupted.” If the retribution is received in this life, it is light and the suffering is less; due to its severity, one swiftly falls into the Avici Hell. The Three Grave Offenses are called ‘grave’ because they are committed against the field of merit, which is heavy. They are: breaking the sangha, killing the Buddha with a malicious mind, and killing an Arhat; killing one's parents is called “grave” because one does not recognize their nurturing kindness. These inverse actions (sin) can only arise in the human realm, not in other realms, because humans have the ability to discern.

Question: Does killing other nobles constitute an inverse action (sin)?

Answer: Killing nobles often leads to falling into hell. Killing an Arhat definitely leads to falling into hell. If someone strikes the Buddha and no blood is drawn, they still incur a heavy sin, because they intended to harm the World-Honored One.

Question: If a person commits one act of filial disobedience, will they fall into hell? If they commit two or three, will they suffer all the consequences in one lifetime?

Answer: Because the sins are numerous, they will suffer severe suffering. In this realm, they will die and be reborn again.

Question: What constitutes a severe offense in the crime of breaking the monastic order?

Answer: If one knows something is not the Dharma but calls it the Dharma, or knows something is the Dharma but calls it not the Dharma, such actions are called severe. If one calls the Dharma not the Dharma, or calls not the Dharma the Dharma, this is inferior to the previous case.

Furthermore, if someone disrupts the Sangha in the presence of the Buddha, claiming to be a great master or the most revered among heavenly beings, this is also considered severe.

Question: If an ordinary person disrupts the Sangha, who is not a noble being, why is it called a severe sin?

Answer: Because it obstructs the true Dharma, it is called a severe sin.

Question: For how long does the disruption of the Sangha last?

Answer: The Dharma does not last long. It does not even last through one night. During this period, the Brahma kings and other heavenly beings, along with Shariputra and the other great disciples, will immediately restore harmony. Some say that these five hundred monks, in their previous lives, obstructed others from attaining the good roots of enlightenment, and now they are receiving this retribution.

Furthermore, ordinary people have light and restless minds, so they are easily destroyed. If one merely attains the worldly understanding of emptiness and the absence of self, it is still not difficult to destroy, let alone the untainted mind. Because evil desires dwell in the mind, one creates the causes for destroying the Sangha. Therefore, those seeking blessings should abandon evil desires.

segments.label: 109 五戒品 (On the Five Precepts | Preceitos)

content.zh:
佛說優婆塞有五戒。
問曰：有人言，具受則得戒律儀。是事云何？

答曰：隨受多少皆得
律儀，但取要有五。
問曰：離繫縛等何故不名為戒，而但說不殺等耶？

答曰：是眷屬
故。
問曰：何故不說斷婬，而但說不邪婬耶？

答曰：白衣處俗難常離
故。又自婬其妻不必墮諸惡趣，如須陀洹等亦行此法，是故不說全
斷婬欲。
問曰：離兩舌等何故不名為戒？

答曰：是事細微難可守護。又兩舌
等是妄語分，若說妄語則已總說。
問曰：飲酒是實罪耶？

答曰：非也。

所以者何？飲酒不為惱眾生
故，但是罪因。若人飲酒則開不善門，是故若教人飲酒則得罪分，
以能障定等諸善法故。如植眾果必為牆障，如是四法是實罪、離為
實福，為守護故結此酒戒。
content.en:
Question: Some say that by fully receiving the precepts, one obtains the discipline of the precepts. How is this?

Answer: Regardless of how many one receives, one obtains the discipline of the precepts, but only the five essential ones are required.

Question: Why are liberation from bonds, etc., not called precepts, but only non-killing, etc., are mentioned?

Answer: Because they are related.

Question: Why is abstaining from sexual misconduct not mentioned, but only non-adultery?

Answer: Because lay people living in the world find it difficult to always abstain.

Moreover, committing adultery with one’s own wife does not necessarily lead to rebirth in the evil realms. Even those who have attained the stage of Sotapanna practice this precept. Therefore, complete abstinence from sexual desire is not mentioned.

Question: Why are refraining from slander and the like not called precepts?

Answer: These matters are subtle and difficult to guard against.

Moreover, slander and the like are part of false speech. If false speech is mentioned, these are already included.

Question: Is drinking alcohol a real sin?

Answer: No. Why? Because drinking alcohol does not harm living beings; it is merely a cause of sin. If a person drinks alcohol, it opens the door to evil deeds. Therefore, if one teaches others to drink alcohol, one commits a sin, as it obstructs the cultivation of good deeds such as concentration. Just as planting various fruits requires a wall as a barrier, these four things are real sins, and abstaining from them is real merit. This is why the precept against drinking alcohol was established for protection.

segments.label: 110 六業品 (On the Six Karmas | Karma)

content.zh:
業有六種，地獄報業、畜生報業、餓鬼報業、人報、天報、不定報
業。
問曰：何者是耶？

答曰：地獄報業，如六足阿毘曇樓炭分中廣說。
又殺生等罪皆為地獄，

如經中說：喜殺生者生地獄中，若得為人則
受短命。乃至邪見亦如是。
問曰：已知十不善道受地獄報，亦生畜生餓鬼及人道中，而汝但說
生地獄及人中，今當別說何業但受地獄報耶？

答曰：即此罪業最重
者受地獄報，小輕則受畜生等報。又若具足三種邪行則為地獄，餘
不具足業為畜生等。又故作重罪則為地獄，又破戒破見人所造惡業
則為地獄。又深心為惡心壞行壞，是人造惡則為地獄。又造不善業
以不善助則為地獄。又若於賢聖造不善業則為地獄。又起不善業不
善修集，如人起不善業，後讚快樂不欲捨離，則為地獄。又以憎恚
心而造罪業則為地獄，若為財物則受餘報。又以邪見心起不善業則
為地獄。又破戒者所作罪業則為地獄。又無慚愧者所作罪業則為地
獄。又惡性人所作罪業則為地獄，譬如濕地小雨成泥。又常行不善
者所作惡業則為地獄。又若無急緣而造惡業則為地獄。又若人不得
空無我分，深染著故，所造罪業則為地獄。又若人不修身戒心慧，
所造惡業則為地獄。又若凡夫人所作罪業則為地獄。

所以者何？是
人不知陰、界、諸入、十二緣等，以不知故，不應作而作、應作而
不作，不應語而語、應語而不語，不應念而念、應念而不念，是人
所作罪業雖少，亦為地獄。又若不見不善中過，是人則能起重罪業
受地獄報。又若人為罪、不依於善，則為地獄，如負債人不依恃
王，債主則得便。又若人善業劣弱，所作少罪亦為地獄，如人身中
火勢微少，得難消食則不能消。又若人但行不善，無善業雜，則為
地獄，如人為賊輕重悉繫。又若捨離一切善根，如象戰時不護惜
手，是人作罪則為地獄。又若行小法、受學小師，是人作罪則為地
獄，如貧賤負債為富貴所牽。又若人常長不善，如負債日息，猶如
屠兒獵師等業，則為地獄。又若覆藏罪則為地獄，如瘡內漏。又若
人不善久住心中，不能疾滅，則為地獄，如被治毒即能殺人。又若
人自作不善亦以教人，開多眾生苦惱門故，則為地獄，如諸國王，
及多知識人行惡邪行令多人學，如富蘭那等。又若所作業多惱眾
生，如燒林等。又教他人令墮非法，如田獵等。又若人以惡業活
命，如賊魁膾屠獵師等。又畢竟破戒人所作罪業則為地獄。至死不
捨故名畢竟，

如偈說：畢竟破戒人，如藤鬘樹枝，是人身造惡，自
令怨得願。又無事而忿，以此忿心而為罪業，則為地獄；若有事而
忿罪則不爾。又以瞋起業，是結重故，則為地獄。

如經中說：瞋為
重罪而易除滅。又若惡心成性則為地獄，若以因緣而起罪業是則輕
微。又若縱逸人所造惡業則為地獄，若為知識所護則得生天上，如
莎婆魁膾臨命終時，舍利弗到其所，是人即以惡眼視舍利弗，不能
令異，呼小來前，更以氣噓之，見舍利弗光色益榮，便生念言：此
人勝我，不可殺也。即以淨心七反上下視舍利弗，以此因緣七生天
上七生人中，後得辟支佛道。又如鴦掘魔羅多起罪業，將欲殺母，
佛為善知識故即得解脫。又如施越以火坑毒飯欲中害佛，佛為善知
識故亦得解脫。如是等人雖有惡業，不墮地獄。故說若縱逸人所作
惡業則為地獄。又若斷善根不可復治，如調達等，猶如病人死相已
現，是人作罪則為地獄。又若人不數為善，將命終時善心難生，是
人心悔故墮地獄。又若臨死時起邪見心，是人以先不善為因、邪見
為緣，故墮地獄。如是多有諸業為地獄報。又論師言，一切不善皆
是地獄因緣，是不善之餘生畜生等中。如經中說，佛語比丘：汝等
所見眾生身邪行口邪行意邪行者，當知便為見地獄人。
問曰：已知地獄報業，畜生報業何者是耶？

答曰：若人雜善起不善
業，故墮畜生。又結使熾盛故墮畜生，如婬欲盛故生於雀鵒鴛鴦等
中，瞋恚盛故生于蚖蛇蝮蠍等中，愚癡熾盛故生猪羊等中，憍逸盛
故生於師子虎狼等中，掉戲盛故生猨猴等中，慳嫉盛故生狗等中，
如是等餘煩惱盛故生種種畜生中。若有少施分者，雖生畜生於中受
樂，如金翅鳥龍象馬等。又口業報多墮畜生，如人不知不信業果報
故起種種口業，如言是人輕躁猶如猨猴，則生猨猴中。若言貪[女*
戾]如鳥、語如狗吠、騃如猪羊、聲如驢鳴、行如駱駝、自高如
象、惡如逸牛、婬如鳥雀、怯如猫狸、諂如野干、便如羖羊、多毛
如牛，起如是等惡口業故，隨業受報。又眾生以貪樂故發種種願，
如樂婬欲則生鳥等中，若聞諸龍金翅鳥等有勢力故願生其中。又經
中說：若於迮狹處死，願得寬處，則生鳥中。若渴死，求水故，生
水中。餓死，貪食故，生廁等中。又從愚癡起輕微業，以雜善故，
生於蚤虱虫蟻等中。又若教他人令墮邪法，則生無智處，盲生盲
死，作死尸中虫。又行雜業故生畜生中，

如經中說：諸畜生隨種種
心，得種種形。又若起應食草業，如人妄語，自呪誓言：若食此食
令我食草、或言食土，如是等。又若人惡口罵言：汝何不食草食
土。是人隨語受生食草土等。又人行不淨施得草等報。又若人觝債
不償，墮牛羊麞鹿驢馬等中償其宿債。如是等業墮畜生中。
問曰：已知畜生報業。以何業故墮餓鬼中？

答曰：於飲食等生慳貪
心，故墮餓鬼。
問曰：若人自物不與，何故得罪？

答曰：是慳人，若人從乞，以貪
惜故則生忿怒，以此罪故生餓鬼中。又此慳人，若人從乞，有而言
無，以妄語故墮餓鬼中。又此人久來修集慳結，見他得利生慳妬心
故墮餓鬼。又此慳人，見他行施則憎恚施主言：此乞者以慣得故，
必當復來從我乞。又從久遠來修集慳心，既自不施亦遮他與。又若
共有物，如寺中僧物及天祠中諸婆羅門物，有人獨惜不欲與人，故
墮餓鬼。又若人劫奪壞他飲食故，生無飲食處。又若人無布施福，
隨所生處報無所得，兼有呵罵乞者業故於中受苦。又此慳者，見人
飢渴無憐愍心，故所生處常受飢渴。如以慈悲得生天上，如是以恚
恨故生惡道中。又深著親屬愛樂住處，故墮迦陵伽等餓鬼中生，以
貪愛是生因緣故。如是等，如《業報經》中廣說。
問曰：已知三惡報業。以何業故生人天中？

答曰：若布施持戒修善
等業，上者生天中、下者生人中，有利根者則生人中，以能行人法
故名為人。又雜善業故生人中。此業有上中下、一心不一心、淨不
淨等。何以知之？以人有種種差品不同故。

如經中說：殺生則短
命、盜竊則貧窮、邪婬則家不貞良、妄語則常被誹謗、兩舌則眷屬
不和、惡口則常聞惡聲、綺語則人不信受、貪嫉則多婬欲、瞋恚則
多惡性、邪見則多愚癡、憍慢則生下賤、自高則矬短、嫉妬則無威
德、慳則貧寒、瞋則醜陋、惱他則多病、雜心布施則嗜不美味、非
時布施則不得隨意、疑悔則生邊地、行不淨施則從苦得報、非道行
婬則得不男形。人中有如是等雜不善業；善業亦與此相違，如不殺
得長壽等。人道中有如是等種種不同，故知是雜業報。又以願故得
生人中，有人不樂放逸亦不多欲，好樂智慧發人身願，則生人中。
又若人好樂供養父母及諸所尊，亦知供養沙門婆羅門等，喜為事業
亦好修福，則生人中。於人中若淨業因緣生欝單越。又若人憎惡田
宅舍廬我所差別，生欝單越。又若人正行白業不惱他，取財而以布
施，亦不貪著，自持戒行又不破戒前後眷屬，則生欝單越。是善小
劣生拘耶尼，又小不如生弗于逮。天報業者是施戒善上淨故生天。
又若人得智慧分，折伏諸結，故生天上。又亦隨雜業故有差別，如
人中說。又以願故，若聞天上受樂因緣，所作善業皆願往生，如八
福生處中說。若行慈悲喜捨，則生梵世乃至有頂。是中禪定有差品
故，報亦差別。若不善斷睡眠調戲等，是人身光則濁，若善除滅光
則明淨。又上善業報則生天，以諸所欲隨念即得故。若離色相得無
色定，則生無色處。如是等名天報業。不定報業者，下善不善業，
是業或地獄、餓鬼、畜生、人天中受。
問曰：餘四道中可得受善業報，地獄云何？

答曰：若小地獄中暫有
停息。如從火地獄得脫，遙見樹林心喜往趣，入此林中，涼風動樹
刀劍未墮，爾時暫樂。或見醎河謂是清水，馳走往趣亦得暫樂。如
是等是地獄中善業報分。是名不定報業。
content.en:
There are six kinds of karma: hell karma, animal karma, hungry ghost karma, human karma, heavenly karma, and indeterminate karma.

Question: What are they?

Answer: Hell karma is as extensively explained in the section on the six-legged Abhidharma and the carbon division.

Furthermore, all sins such as killing are hell, as stated in the sutra: “Those who delight in killing are born in hell; if they are reborn as humans, they will have short lives.” The same applies to wrong views.

Question: We already know that the ten unwholesome paths lead to hell, and that beings are also reborn as animals, hungry ghosts, and humans. Yet you only mention being born in hell and as humans. What other karma leads solely to hell?

Answer: The most severe of these sins lead to hellish retribution, while lesser ones lead to rebirth as animals, etc.

Furthermore, if one fully possesses the three evil deeds, one is destined for hell; those who lack these are reborn as animals, etc. Additionally, intentionally committing grave sins leads to hell, as does breaking precepts or views and committing evil deeds.

Moreover, those with a deeply evil mind and corrupted conduct who commit evil deeds are destined for hell.

Furthermore, committing unwholesome deeds with unwholesome aids leads to hell.

Furthermore, if one commits unwholesome deeds toward the wise and noble, one will be reborn in hell. If one engages in unwholesome deeds without proper cultivation, such as praising pleasure and refusing to abandon it, one will be reborn in hell. If one commits sins out of hatred, one will be reborn in hell; if done for wealth, one will receive other retributions. If one commits unwholesome deeds out of wrong views, one will be reborn in hell. If one breaks precepts, one will be reborn in hell.

Furthermore, those who commit evil deeds without shame and remorse will go to hell. Those with an evil nature will go to hell, like wet ground turning to mud in the rain. Those who constantly engage in evil deeds will go to hell. Those who commit evil deeds without urgent cause will go to hell. Those who cannot attain emptiness and selflessness, and are deeply attached to the self, will go to hell.

Furthermore, if a person does not cultivate morality, precepts, mindfulness, and discernment, the evil deeds they commit lead to hell.

Furthermore, the evil deeds committed by ordinary beings lead to hell. Why is this so? Because such people do not understand the five aggregates, the twelve sense bases, and the twelve links of dependent origination. Due to their ignorance, they do what they should not do, fail to do what they should do, speak when they should not speak, remain silent when they should speak, think what they should not think, and fail to think what they should think. Even if the evil deeds they commit are few, they still lead to hell.

Furthermore, if one fails to recognize the faults of evil deeds, one may commit grave sins and suffer the retribution of hell.

Furthermore, if a person commits sins without relying on goodness, they will be sent to hell. This is like a debtor who does not rely on the king, allowing the creditor to take advantage of the situation. If a person’s good karma is weak, even if they commit few sins, they will be sent to hell. This is like a person with a weak fire in their body who cannot digest food easily. If a person only does evil and has no good karma to offset it, they will be sent to hell. This is like a thief who is bound with light chains.

Furthermore, if one abandons all virtuous roots, like an elephant in battle that does not protect its hands, such a person, when committing sins, will be reborn in hell. If one practices minor teachings or studies under a minor teacher, such a person, when committing sins, will be reborn in hell, like a poor and indebted person being dragged by the wealthy. If one constantly engages in evil deeds, like a debtor accumulating daily interest, or like the professions of a butcher or hunter, such a person will be reborn in hell.

Furthermore, if one conceals sins, one will be reborn in hell, like a wound that festers. If one harbors evil intentions in the mind for a long time and cannot quickly eliminate them, one will be reborn in hell, like a poison that can kill upon ingestion. If one commits evil deeds oneself and also teaches others to do so, opening the gates of suffering for many beings, one will be reborn in hell, like kings or influential people who engage in evil deeds and lead others to follow them, such as the wealthy man who sold his son.

Furthermore, if one’s actions cause great suffering to sentient beings, such as burning a forest, or if one teaches others to fall into unlawful conduct, such as hunting, or if one sustains one’s life through evil deeds, such as being a bandit leader or a butcher, or if one completely breaks one’s precepts, the sins committed are hell. Because they do not abandon their evil deeds until death, they are called “ultimately destroyed.” As the verse says: “Those who utterly break their vows are like the branches of a vine tree; they create evil in the human body and bring about their own enemies' desires.”

Furthermore, if one becomes angry without cause and commits evil deeds out of anger, one will be reborn in hell. If one becomes angry for a valid reason, it is not the same. If one commits evil deeds out of anger, it is a heavy karmic bond, and one will be reborn in hell. As the sutra says: Anger is a heavy sin but easy to eliminate. If evil intentions become one's nature, one will be reborn in hell; if one commits sins due to circumstances, the karma is lighter.

Furthermore, if one indulges in evil deeds, one will be reborn in hell. However, if one is protected by a wise teacher, one may be reborn in heaven. For example, when Shāpa Kuīhuì was about to die, Śāriputra came to him. The man looked at Śāriputra with a hostile gaze but could not change his expression. He called Śāriputra to come closer and blew on him. Seeing that Śāriputra’s complexion became even more radiant, he thought, “This person is superior to me; I cannot kill him.” He then looked at Shariputra with a pure mind seven times. Because of this cause and effect, he was reborn seven times in heaven and seven times as a human being, and eventually attained the path of a Pratyekabuddha. Again, like Angulimala, who committed evil deeds and was about to kill his mother, the Buddha acted as his good friend and thus he was liberated. Again, like Shiyue, who used a pit filled with poisonous food to harm the Buddha, the Buddha acted as his good friend and thus he was liberated. Such people, though they have committed evil deeds, do not fall into hell. Therefore, it is said that if one indulges in evil deeds, one will fall into hell. Again, if one cuts off the roots of goodness and cannot be reformed, like Devadatta, it is like a sick person whose death is imminent. Such a person, if he commits evil deeds, will fall into hell. Again, if a person does not frequently perform good deeds, when his life is about to end, it is difficult for a good mind to arise; such a person, because of his regret, falls into hell.

Furthermore, if one harbors wrong views at the moment of death, such a person, due to previous unwholesome deeds as the cause and wrong views as the condition, will fall into hell. Thus, there are many kinds of karma that result in hell as retribution. The commentator also states that all unwholesome deeds are the causes and conditions for hell, and the remainder of unwholesome karma is reborn as animals or other beings. As the sutra says, the Buddha told the monks: “You should know that all beings you see who engage in wrong conduct with their body, speech, and mind are those who will see hell.”

Question: Having understood the karmic retribution of hell, what is the karmic retribution of the animal realm?

Answer: If a person mixes good deeds with evil deeds, they will fall into the animal realm. Additionally, if the defilements are intense, they will fall into the animal realm. For example, intense lust leads to rebirth as birds like sparrows, magpies, or mandarin ducks; intense anger leads to rebirth as snakes, scorpions, or centipedes; Those with intense ignorance are reborn as pigs or sheep. Those with intense arrogance are reborn as lions, tigers, or wolves. Those with intense playfulness are reborn as monkeys. Those with intense greed and jealousy are reborn as dogs. Similarly, those with intense other afflictions are reborn as various animals. If one has even a little merit from giving, they may be reborn as animals that enjoy happiness, such as garudas, dragons, elephants, or horses.

Furthermore, those with many verbal karmic retributions fall into the animal realm. For example, those who do not understand or believe in the consequences of karma and commit various verbal offenses, such as saying, “This person is as restless as a monkey,” will be reborn as monkeys. If one says, "Greedy like a bird, speaks like a dog barking, foolish like pigs and sheep, sounds like a donkey braying, walks like a camel, arrogant like an elephant, vicious like a wild ox, lustful like birds and sparrows, cowardly like cats and foxes, deceitful like jackals, stubborn like goats, hairy like cows, and so on. Due to such evil verbal karma, one receives retribution according to one's karma.

Furthermore, sentient beings, driven by greed and desire, make various vows. For example, those who delight in lustful desires are reborn among birds, and those who hear of the power of dragons and Garuda birds wish to be reborn among them.

Furthermore, the sutra states: If one dies in a narrow place, wishing for a spacious place, one is reborn as a bird. If one dies of thirst, seeking water, one is reborn in water. If one dies of hunger, craving food, one is reborn in latrines or similar places. Additionally, due to minor karma arising from ignorance, combined with various virtuous deeds, one is reborn as fleas, lice, ants, or similar beings.

Furthermore, if one teaches others to fall into evil ways, one will be reborn in a place of ignorance, blind and deaf, and become a worm in a corpse. Due to mixed karma, one is reborn among animals, as the sutra says: “All animals, according to their various minds, take on various forms.” If one commits the karma of eating grass, such as a person who falsely vows, “If I eat this food, may I eat grass,” or says, “Eat earth,” and so on. If one uses harsh words to scold others, saying, “Why don't you eat grass or soil?” that person will be reborn according to their words and eat grass or soil. If one performs impure acts of generosity, one will receive grass as a result. If one fails to repay debts, one will be reborn as cattle, sheep, deer, donkeys, or horses to repay past debts. Such actions lead to rebirth in the animal realm.

Question: We have understood the karmic consequences of rebirth in the animal realm. What karma leads to rebirth as a hungry ghost?

Answer: Greed for food and other things leads to rebirth as a hungry ghost.

Question: If a person does not give what belongs to others, why is that a sin?

Answer: A greedy person, when someone begs, becomes angry out of greed, and because of this sin, is reborn as a hungry ghost.

Furthermore, this miserly person, when someone begs from them, lies and says they have something, and thus falls into the hungry ghost realm due to false speech. Additionally, this person has cultivated miserliness over a long period of time, and when they see others gain benefits, they become jealous and thus fall into the hungry ghost realm.

Furthermore, this miserly person, when they see others making offerings, hates the donor and thinks, “This beggar is accustomed to receiving, so they will surely come back to beg from me again.”

Furthermore, having cultivated stinginess over a long period of time, they neither give nor prevent others from giving. If there are shared possessions, such as the property of monks in a monastery or the possessions of Brahmins in a temple, and someone selfishly refuses to share them with others, they are reborn as hungry ghosts. If someone steals or destroys others' food, they are reborn in a place where there is no food.

Furthermore, if a person lacks the merit of generosity, wherever they are reborn, they receive nothing in return, and due to the karma of scolding beggars, they suffer in that realm.

Moreover, those who are stingy, upon seeing others hungry and thirsty, lack compassion, so wherever they are reborn, they constantly suffer from hunger and thirst. Just as one attains birth in heaven through compassion, so too does one be born in the evil realms due to hatred and anger.

Furthermore, those deeply attached to their relatives and their place of residence fall into the hungry ghost realm, such as the Kalavinka, because greed and attachment are the causes of their birth. Such examples are extensively explained in the Sutra on the Retribution of Karma.

Question: Having understood the three evil retributions, by what karma are beings born into the human and heavenly realms?

Answer: If one practices generosity, morality, and other virtuous deeds, those of the highest level are reborn in heaven, those of the lower level are reborn among humans, and those with sharp faculties are reborn among humans because they are capable of practicing the Dharma. Additionally, one is reborn among humans due to mixed virtuous deeds. These deeds have upper, middle, and lower levels, as well as single-minded and non-single-minded, pure and impure, and so on. How do we know this? Because humans have various differences and distinctions. As the sutra says: Killing leads to a short life; stealing leads to poverty; adultery leads to an unfaithful family; lying leads to constant slander; gossip leads to discord among relatives; harsh words lead to hearing unpleasant sounds; frivolous speech leads to others not trusting you; greed and jealousy lead to excessive desire; anger leads to a vicious nature; wrong views lead to ignorance and stupidity; arrogance leads to lowly birth, self-importance leads to short stature, jealousy leads to lack of virtue, stinginess leads to poverty, anger leads to ugliness, harming others leads to many illnesses, giving with a divided mind leads to a taste for unpleasant food, giving at the wrong time leads to inability to give as one wishes, doubt and regret lead to birth in borderlands, impure giving leads to suffering. Engaging in immoral sexual conduct leads to being born without male characteristics. Among humans, there are such various unwholesome karma; wholesome karma is the opposite of this, such as not killing leads to a long life, etc. In the human realm, there are such various differences, hence it is known as the result of mixed karma.

Furthermore, due to one’s vows, one is reborn among humans. Some people do not delight in indulgence or have many desires. They delight in discernment and aspire to be reborn as humans, thus they are reborn among humans.

Furthermore, if one delights in honoring one’s parents and all those who are respected, and also knows how to honor monks and Brahmins, and is joyful in one’s work and eager to cultivate merit, one is reborn among humans. Among humans, if one is born with pure karma, one is reborn in the human realm. If one hates and despises fields, houses, dwellings, and possessions, one is reborn in the human realm.

Furthermore, if a person practices virtuous deeds, does not harm others, acquires wealth and distributes it generously, is not greedy, upholds the precepts, and does not break them, even if their relatives do so, they will be reborn in the lower realms. This is a minor merit, leading to rebirth in the Kāyāṇī realm. If the merit is even smaller, they will be reborn in the Avīci realm. Those who practice generosity and morality will be reborn in heaven due to the purity of these virtues.

Furthermore, if a person attains discernment and overcomes all attachments, they are reborn in heaven. There are also differences due to various karma, as explained in the human realm. Additionally, due to their vows, if they hear about the causes and conditions for enjoying the pleasures of heaven and dedicate all their good deeds toward rebirth there, as explained in the Eight Auspicious Birthplaces, they will be reborn in the Brahma realm up to the highest realm. If they practice compassion, joy, and generosity, they will be reborn in the Brahma realm up to the highest realm. Within this, there are different levels of meditation, so the rewards also differ. If one fails to cut off sleep and frivolity, the light of the human body becomes turbid. If one skillfully eliminates them, the light becomes clear and pure. Those with superior good karma are reborn in heaven, as whatever they desire is immediately attained. If one attains the formless realm by transcending form, one is reborn in the formless realm. Such are the heavenly rewards of karma. Those with indeterminate karma are those with inferior good or evil karma, which may be reborn in hell, the hungry ghost realm, the animal realm, or the human and heavenly realms.

Question: In the remaining four realms, can one receive the rewards of good karma? What about hell?

Answer: If there is a temporary respite in a minor hell, such as escaping from a fiery hell and seeing a forest in the distance, one may rejoice and head toward it. Upon entering the forest, the cool breeze rustles the trees, and the swords have not yet fallen, bringing temporary joy. Or one may see a salty river and mistake it for fresh water, rushing toward it and also experiencing temporary joy. Such are the rewards of good karma within hell. This is called the indeterminate retribution of karma.
