He called Śāriputra to come closer and blew on him. Seeing that Śāriputra’s complexion became even more radiant, he thought, “This person is superior to me; I cannot kill him.” He then looked at Shariputra with a pure mente seven times. Because of this cause and effect, he was reborn seven times in heaven and seven times as a human being, and eventually attained the path of a Pratyekabuddha. Again, like Angulimala, who committed evil deeds and was about to kill his mother, the Buda acted as his good friend and thus he was liberated. Again, like Shiyue, who used a pit filled with poisonous food to harm the Buda, the Buda acted as his good friend and thus he was liberated. Such people, though they have committed evil deeds, do not fall into hell. Therefore, it is said that if one indulges in evil deeds, one will fall into hell. Again, if one cuts off the roots of goodness and cannot be reformed, like Devadatta, it is like a sick person whose death is imminent. Such a person, if he commits evil deeds, will fall into hell. Again, if a person does not frequently perform good deeds, when his life is about to end, it is difficult for a good mente to arise; such a person, because of his regret, falls into hell.

Furthermore, if one harbors wrong views at the moment of death, such a person, due to previous unwholesome deeds as the cause and wrong views as the condition, will fall into hell. Thus, there are many kinds of karma that result in hell as retribution. The commentator also states that all unwholesome deeds are the causes and conditions for hell, and the remainder of unwholesome karma is reborn as animals or other beings. As the sutra says, the Buda told the monks: “You should know that all beings you see who engage in wrong conduct with their corpo, speech, and mente are those who will see hell.”

Question: Having understood the karmic retribution of hell, what is the karmic retribution of the animal realm?

Answer: If a person mixes good deeds with evil deeds, they will fall into the animal realm. Additionally, if the defilements are intense, they will fall into the animal realm. For example, intense lust leads to rebirth as birds like sparrows, magpies, or mandarin ducks; intense anger leads to rebirth as snakes, scorpions, or centipedes; Those with intense ignorance are reborn as pigs or sheep. Those with intense arrogance are reborn as lions, tigers, or wolves. Those with intense playfulness are reborn as monkeys. Those with intense greed and jealousy are reborn as dogs. Similarly, those with intense other afflictions are reborn as various animals. If one has even a little merit from giving, they may be reborn as animals that enjoy happiness, such as garudas, dragons, elephants, or horses.

Furthermore, those with many verbal karmic retributions fall into the animal realm. For example, those who do not understand or believe in the consequences of karma and commit various verbal offenses, such as saying, “This person is as restless as a monkey,” will be reborn as monkeys. If one says, "Greedy like a bird, speaks like a dog barking, foolish like pigs and sheep, sounds like a donkey braying, walks like a camel, arrogant like an elephant, vicious like a wild ox, lustful like birds and sparrows, cowardly like cats and foxes, deceitful like jackals, stubborn like goats, hairy like cows, and so on. Due to such evil verbal karma, one receives retribution according to one's karma.

Furthermore, sentient beings, driven by greed and desire, make various vows. For example, those who delight in lustful desires are reborn among birds, and those who hear of the power of dragons and Garuda birds wish to be reborn among them.

Furthermore, the sutra states: If one dies in a narrow place, wishing for a spacious place, one is reborn as a bird. If one dies of thirst, seeking water, one is reborn in water. If one dies of hunger, craving food, one is reborn in latrines or similar places. Additionally, due to minor karma arising from ignorance, combined with various virtuous deeds, one is reborn as fleas, lice, ants, or similar beings.

Furthermore, if one teaches others to fall into evil ways, one will be reborn in a place of ignorance, blind and deaf, and become a worm in a corpse. Due to mixed karma, one is reborn among animals, as the sutra says: “All animals, according to their various minds, take on various forms.” If one commits the karma of eating grass, such as a person who falsely vows, “If I eat this food, may I eat grass,” or says, “Eat earth,” and so on. If one uses harsh words to scold others, saying, “Why don't you eat grass or soil?” that person will be reborn according to their words and eat grass or soil. If one performs impure acts of generosity, one will receive grass as a result. If one fails to repay debts, one will be reborn as cattle, sheep, deer, donkeys, or horses to repay past debts. Such actions lead to rebirth in the animal realm.

Question: We have understood the karmic consequences of rebirth in the animal realm. What karma leads to rebirth as a hungry ghost?

Answer: Greed for food and other things leads to rebirth as a hungry ghost.

Question: If a person does not give what belongs to others, why is that a sin?

Answer: A greedy person, when someone begs, becomes angry out of greed, and because of this sin, is reborn as a hungry ghost.

Furthermore, this miserly person, when someone begs from them, lies and says they have something, and thus falls into the hungry ghost realm due to false speech. Additionally, this person has cultivated miserliness over a long period of time, and when they see others gain benefits, they become jealous and thus fall into the hungry ghost realm.

Furthermore, this miserly person, when they see others making offerings, hates the donor and thinks, “This beggar is accustomed to receiving, so they will surely come back to beg from me again.”

Furthermore, having cultivated stinginess over a long period of time, they neither give nor prevent others from giving. If there are shared possessions, such as the property of monks in a monastery or the possessions of Brahmins in a temple, and someone selfishly refuses to share them with others, they are reborn as hungry ghosts. If someone steals or destroys others' food, they are reborn in a place where there is no food.

Furthermore, if a person lacks the merit of generosity, wherever they are reborn, they receive nothing in return, and due to the karma of scolding beggars, they suffer in that realm.

Moreover, those who are stingy, upon seeing others hungry and thirsty, lack compassion, so wherever they are reborn, they constantly suffer from hunger and thirst. Just as one attains birth in heaven through compassion, so too does one be born in the evil realms due to hatred and anger.

Furthermore, those deeply attached to their relatives and their place of residence fall into the hungry ghost realm, such as the Kalavinka, because greed and attachment are the causes of their birth. Such examples are extensively explained in the Sutra on the Retribution of Karma.

Question: Having understood the three evil retributions, by what karma are beings born into the human and heavenly realms?

Answer: If one practices generosity, morality, and other virtuous deeds, those of the highest level are reborn in heaven, those of the lower level are reborn among humans, and those with sharp faculties are reborn among humans because they are capable of practicing the Dharma. Additionally, one is reborn among humans due to mixed virtuous deeds. These deeds have upper, middle, and lower levels, as well as single-minded and non-single-minded, pure and impure, and so on. How do we know this? Because humans have various differences and distinctions. As the sutra says: Killing leads to a short life; stealing leads to poverty; adultery leads to an unfaithful family; lying leads to constant slander; gossip leads to discord among relatives; harsh words lead to hearing unpleasant sounds; frivolous speech leads to others not trusting you; greed and jealousy lead to excessive desire; anger leads to a vicious nature; wrong views lead to ignorance and stupidity; arrogance leads to lowly birth, self-importance leads to short stature, jealousy leads to lack of virtue, stinginess leads to poverty, anger leads to ugliness, harming others leads to many illnesses, giving with a divided mente leads to a taste for unpleasant food, giving at the wrong time leads to inability to give as one wishes, doubt and regret lead to birth in borderlands, impure giving leads to sofrimento (duḥkha). Engaging in immoral sexual conduct leads to being born without male characteristics. Among humans, there are such various unwholesome karma; wholesome karma is the opposite of this, such as not killing leads to a long life, etc. In the human realm, there are such various differences, hence it is known as the result of mixed karma.

Furthermore, due to one’s vows, one is reborn among humans. Some people do not delight in indulgence or have many desires. They delight in discernment and aspire to be reborn as humans, thus they are reborn among humans.

Furthermore, if one delights in honoring one’s parents and all those who are respected, and also knows how to honor monks and Brahmins, and is joyful in one’s work and eager to cultivate merit, one is reborn among humans. Among humans, if one is born with pure karma, one is reborn in the human realm. If one hates and despises fields, houses, dwellings, and possessions, one is reborn in the human realm.

Furthermore, if a person practices virtuous deeds, does not harm others, acquires wealth and distributes it generously, is not greedy, upholds the precepts, and does not break them, even if their relatives do so, they will be reborn in the lower realms. This is a minor merit, leading to rebirth in the Kāyāṇī realm. If the merit is even smaller, they will be reborn in the Avīci realm. Those who practice generosity and morality will be reborn in heaven due to the purity of these virtues.

Furthermore, if a person attains discernment and overcomes all attachments, they are reborn in heaven. There are also differences due to various karma, as explained in the human realm. Additionally, due to their vows, if they hear about the causes and conditions for enjoying the pleasures of heaven and dedicate all their good deeds toward rebirth there, as explained in the Eight Auspicious Birthplaces, they will be reborn in the Brahma realm up to the highest realm. If they practice compassion, joy, and generosity, they will be reborn in the Brahma realm up to the highest realm. Within this, there are different levels of meditation, so the rewards also differ. If one fails to cut off sleep and frivolity, the light of the human corpo becomes turbid. If one skillfully eliminates them, the light becomes clear and pure. Those with superior good karma are reborn in heaven, as whatever they desire is immediately attained. If one attains the formless realm by transcending form, one is reborn in the formless realm. Such are the heavenly rewards of karma. Those with indeterminate karma are those with inferior good or evil karma, which may be reborn in hell, the hungry ghost realm, the animal realm, or the human and heavenly realms.

Question: In the remaining four realms, can one receive the rewards of good karma? What about hell?

Answer: If there is a temporary respite in a minor hell, such as escaping from a fiery hell and seeing a forest in the distance, one may rejoice and head toward it. Upon entering the forest, the cool breeze rustles the trees, and the swords have not yet fallen, bringing temporary joy. Or one may see a salty river and mistake it for fresh water, rushing toward it and also experiencing temporary joy. Such are the rewards of good karma within hell. This is called the indeterminate retribution of karma.

segments.label: 111 七不善律儀品 (On the Seven Unwholesome Precepts | Preceitos)

content.zh:
七不善律儀，謂殺、盜、邪婬、兩舌、惡口、妄言、綺語。若人於
此七事，若具足若不具足，皆名不善律儀人。
問曰：何者成就不善律儀？

答曰：成就殺不善律儀，謂屠殺等。成
就盜者，謂劫賊等。成就邪婬，謂非道行婬及婬女等。成就妄語，
謂歌舞伎兒等。成就兩舌，謂喜讒謗及讀誦讒書、遘合國事等。成
就惡口，謂獄卒等，亦以惡口自活命等。成就綺語，謂合集言辭令
人笑等。有人言，諸王宰將治王事者，常成就此不善律儀。是事不
然。

所以者何？若人作罪相續不息，是名成就不善律儀，王等不
爾。
問曰：云何得此不善律儀？

答曰：隨行惡業時得。
問曰：為從所殺眾生得此律儀、為從一切眾生得耶？

答曰：從一切
眾生得。如人持戒，於一切眾生得善律儀，不善律儀亦如是。若隨
殺眾生，得二種無作：一殺罪所攝、二不善律儀所攝，於餘眾生得
不善律儀所攝。
問曰：是不善律儀幾時成就？

答曰：乃至未得捨心則常成就。
問曰：若人從下軟心得不善律儀，若貪等心得，是人常如是成就，
為更得耶？

答曰：隨心隨煩惱因緣更得。此不善律儀念念常得，於
一切眾生得起七種，是七種有上中下故有二十一種，如是念念常於
一切眾生邊得。
問曰：是不善律儀云何得捨？

答曰：隨受善律儀時捨，死時亦捨。
又發深心從今日更不復作，爾時亦捨。有論師言，轉根時捨。是事
不然。

所以者何？不能男等亦得成就。比尼中亦說，若比丘轉根不
失律儀。當知不以轉根故捨。
問曰：五道中何道眾生成就不善律儀？

答曰：但人成就，不在餘
道。有人言，師子虎狼等常以惡業活命，亦應成就。
content.en:
The seven unwholesome precepts are killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, slander, harsh speech, false speech, and frivolous speech. If a person commits any of these seven acts, whether completely or partially, they are called a person who has committed unwholesome precepts.

Question: What constitutes the fulfillment of unwholesome precepts?

Answer: The fulfillment of the unwholesome precept of killing includes acts such as slaughtering animals. To accomplish theft is to commit robbery, etc. To accomplish sexual misconduct is to engage in sexual relations outside of marriage or with a prostitute, etc. To accomplish false speech is to engage in singing and dancing, etc. To accomplish divisive speech is to delight in slander and reading slanderous books, or to discuss state affairs, etc. To accomplish harsh speech is to be a jailer, etc., or to use harsh speech to sustain one's life, etc. The achievement of frivolous speech refers to combining words to make others laugh, etc. Some say that kings, ministers, and those who govern the affairs of the king always achieve these unwholesome precepts. This is not the case. Why is that? If a person continuously commits sins without ceasing, that is called achieving unwholesome precepts. Kings and others are not like that.

Question: How does one obtain these unwholesome precepts?

Answer: They are obtained through performing evil deeds.

Question: Is this precept obtained from the beings one has killed, or from all beings?

Answer: It is obtained from all beings. Just as one who keeps the precepts obtains good precepts from all beings, so too with evil precepts. If one kills beings, one obtains two kinds of non-action. One kind is encompassed by the sin of killing, and the other is encompassed by evil precepts. From other beings, one obtains evil precepts.

Question: When is this unwholesome precept accomplished?

Answer: It is constantly accomplished until one attains the mind of renunciation.

Question: If a person obtains the unwholesome precept from a lower, soft mind, or from a mind of greed, etc., does this person constantly accomplish it in this way, or does he obtain it again?

Answer: It is obtained again according to the mind and the causes and conditions of defilements. This unwholesome precept is constantly attained in every moment, and seven kinds arise toward all sentient beings. These seven kinds have upper, middle, and lower levels, thus there are twenty-one kinds. In this way, they are constantly attained toward all sentient beings in every moment.

Question: How is the unwholesome precept abandoned?

Answer: It is abandoned when one receives the wholesome precept, and also at the time of death. Additionally, if one vows with a deep resolve from this day forward never to commit it again, it is also abandoned at that time. Some scholars say it is abandoned when the roots  are transformed. This is not the case. Why? Because even those who cannot become men can achieve it. The Vinaya also states that if a monk changes his roots  but does not lose his precepts, he does not abandon them. Therefore, it is not abandoned due to changing one's roots .

Question: In the five realms, which realm's beings achieve unwholesome precepts?

Answer: Only humans achieve them; they are not found in the other realms. Some say that lions, tigers, wolves, and other such beings, who sustain their lives through evil deeds, should also achieve them.

segments.label: 112 七善律儀品 (On the Seven Virtues of Moral Discipline | Virtude)

content.zh:
七善律儀，不殺乃至不綺語。
問曰：於非眾生數得是善律儀不？

答曰：得，但要因眾生。是善律
儀三種，戒律儀、禪律儀、定律儀。
問曰：何故不說無漏律儀？

答曰：無漏律儀在後二中攝，故不別
說。有論師言，更有斷律儀，謂離欲界時得善律儀。以斷破戒等惡
故名曰斷，而實一切律儀皆三中攝。
問曰：諸外道等得此戒律儀耶？

答曰：得，此人亦以深心離諸惡
故。戒師教言：汝從今日不應起殺等罪。
問曰：餘道眾生得此戒律儀不？

答曰：經中說，諸龍等亦能受一日
戒。故知應有。
問曰：有人言，不能男等無戒律儀。是事云何？

答曰：是戒律儀從
心邊生，不能男等亦有善心，何故不得？
問曰：何故不聽作比丘耶？

答曰：是人結使深厚難得道故。又此人
不在比丘中，亦不在比丘尼中，是故不聽。又彼中亦遮餘人，如睞
眼等，是人亦得此善律儀。
問曰：比尼中遮逆罪者、賊住者、污比丘尼等，不聽作比丘。是諸
人等亦有善律儀耶？

答曰：是人若為白衣，或得善律儀，如不遮此
人修行布施慈等善法。如是若有世間戒律儀者，有何咎耶？但以是
人為惡業所污亦障聖道，是故不聽出家。
問曰：為從可殺等眾生得善律儀、為於一切眾生得耶？

答曰：皆於
一切眾生邊得。若不爾，律儀則有分，有分則不具足。又此律儀則
可增減，亦同尼延子法，謂百由旬內不殺生等。有此等過，是故律
儀無有分別。若有人言，我於此人離殺、此人不離。是人不得此戒
律儀。有論師言，若分別布施行慈心等有福德，戒亦可爾，如持一
戒亦得戒福，如是於一眾生亦得律儀。
問曰：是戒律儀二種，一盡形、二一日一夜。盡形者，若比丘、優
婆塞。一日一夜者，如受八戒。一日一夜是事云何？

答曰：是事無
定，若一日一夜、若但一日、或但一夜、若半日、或半夜，隨能受
時得，出家則但應盡形。若言我但一月二月、若但一歲，則不名得
出家法。五戒亦爾。
問曰：若得善律儀，還破失律儀不？

答曰：不失，但以不善法污此
律儀。
問曰：但於現在眾生得戒律儀、為從三世眾生得耶？

答曰：皆於三
世眾生所得。如人供養過去所尊亦有福德，律儀亦爾。是故一切諸
佛同一戒品，是律儀無量。如於一眾生得起七種，從不貪等善根起
故，亦從上中下心起故，故有多種。如一人，一切眾生邊亦如是，
念念常得故有無量。
問曰：戒律儀幾時可得？

答曰：有人受一日戒是初律儀，即日受優
婆塞戒是第二律儀，即日出家作沙彌是第三律儀，即日受具足戒是
第四律儀，即日得禪定是第五律儀，即日得無色定是第六律儀，即
日得無漏是第七律儀。隨得道果處更得律儀，而本得不失，但勝者
受名。如是則福德益增，以此戒律儀於一切眾生念念常得，故說一
日戒律儀，四大寶藏不及十六分中之一。禪律儀、無漏律儀隨心
行，戒律儀不隨心行。
問曰：有人言，入定時有禪律儀，出定則無。是事云何？

答曰：出
入常有，是人得實不作惡法，與破戒相違，常不為惡、善心轉勝，
故應常有。
問曰：若禪無色中無破戒法，以何相違名善律儀？

答曰：法應如
是，諸仙聖人皆得善律儀。若以破戒相違故有律儀者，則但應從可
惱眾生所得善律儀。有如是咎，是故不然。
content.en:
The seven virtues of moral discipline are: not killing, not stealing, not lying, not slandering, not consuming intoxicants, not engaging in sexual misconduct, and not taking life.

Question: Can these virtues of moral discipline be attained by non-sentient beings?

Answer: Yes, but they must be conditioned by sentient beings. These virtues of moral discipline are of three kinds: precepts, meditation, and samadhi.

Question: Why are the precepts of the path to liberation not mentioned?

Answer: The precepts of the path to liberation are included in the latter two, so they are not mentioned separately. Some scholars say there is also the precept of extinction, which is attained when one leaves the desire's realm. It is called “extinction” because it breaks the evil of breaking precepts, but in reality, all precepts are included in the three categories.

Question: Do heretics attain this precept of morality?

Answer: Yes, because they also abandon all evils with a deep mind. The precept-giver instructs: “From today onward, you should not commit the sins of killing, etc.”

Question: Do beings of other paths obtain these precepts and disciplinary rules?

Answer: The sutras state that even dragons can receive the precepts for one day. Therefore, it should be possible.

Question: Some say that those who cannot be men have no precepts or disciplinary rules. How is this to be understood?

Answer: These precepts and disciplinary rules arise from the mind. Those who cannot be men also have a good mind. Why should they not obtain them?

Question: Why are they not permitted to become monks?

Answer: Because such people have deep-rooted defilements and find it difficult to attain the path.

Moreover, such people are neither monks nor nuns, so they are not permitted. Additionally, in that order, others are also prohibited, such as those with eye defects, yet such people can still receive this virtuous precepts.

Question: In the Vinaya, those who commit perverse offense, dwell as thieves, or defile nuns are not permitted to become monks. Do such people also possess virtuous precepts?

Answer: If such a person is a layperson or has obtained good precepts, they are not prohibited from practicing virtuous deeds such as generosity and compassion. If there are those in the world who have precepts, what fault is there in that? It is merely because such a person is defiled by evil karma and obstructed from the noble path, hence they are not permitted to ordain.

Question: Do good precepts obtained from beings that may be killed apply to all beings?

Answer: They apply to all beings. If not, then the precepts would be divided. If divided, they would not be complete.

Furthermore, these precepts could be increased or decreased, similar to the teachings of the Niyana sect, which states that within a hundred yojanas one should not kill living beings, etc. Such flaws exist, therefore the precepts have no distinctions. If someone says, “I have abandoned killing toward this person, but this person has not abandoned it,” then this person has not obtained this precept. Some scholars say that if one distinguishes between the merits of giving, practicing compassion, etc., and the precepts, the precepts can also be distinguished. For example, by keeping one precept, one obtains the merit of the precept. Similarly, by keeping one precept for one being, one obtains the precepts.

Question: Are there two kinds of precepts and precepts—one for a lifetime and one for a day and night? The one for a lifetime refers to monks and laypeople. The one for a day and night refers to taking the eight precepts. How is this for a day and night?

Answer: This is not fixed. It may be one day and one night, or just one day, or just one night, or half a day, or half a night. It is obtained according to one's ability to receive it for 118 hours. Those who have renounced the world should only vow for the duration of their lives. If one says, “I will only vow for one month or two months, or just one year,” this is not called obtaining the monastic precepts. The five precepts are the same.

Question: If one obtains good precepts, can they be broken and lost?

Answer: It is not lost, but it is defiled by unwholesome actions.

Question: Does one obtain the precepts and discipline only from present beings, or from beings of the three past lives?

Answer: They are obtained from beings of the three past lives. Just as one gains merit by offering to those one respected in the past, so too with the precepts and discipline. Therefore, all Buddhas share the same precepts, and the precepts are immeasurable. For example, if one gains seven kinds of precepts from a single being, this arises from the good roots  of non-greed, etc., and also from the upper, middle, and lower minds, hence there are many kinds. Similarly, one person can gain precepts from all beings, and since this is attained moment by moment, there are innumerable kinds.

Question: When can the precepts be attained?

Answer: Some receive the one-day precepts as the first discipline, then on the same day receive the layperson’s precepts as the second discipline, then on the same day ordain as a novice monk as the third discipline, then on the same day receive the full precepts as the fourth discipline, then on the same day attain samadhi as the fifth discipline, then on the same day attain the formless realm as the sixth discipline, and then on the same day attain the extinction of defilements as the seventh discipline. Depending on where one attains the fruit of the path, one further attains the discipline, but the original discipline is not lost; only the superior one is named. In this way, merit and virtue increase. With this precept and discipline, all beings constantly attain it in every moment, hence it is said that the precepts of one day surpass the four great treasures by more than sixteen parts. The discipline of meditation and the discipline of nirvana follow the mind, while the discipline of precepts does not follow the mind.

Question: Some say that during meditation there is the discipline of meditation, but upon emerging from meditation it ceases. How is this to be understood?

Answer: They are always present. This person has attained the truth and does not commit evil deeds, which contradicts breaking precepts. They always refrain from evil and their virtuous mind grows stronger, so they should always be present.

Question: If there are no broken precepts in meditation or the formless realm, what contradicts them to be called virtuous precepts?

Answer: The Dharma should be like this. All sages and nobles attain virtuous precepts. If one were to say that precepts exist because they are contrary to breaking precepts, then one should only obtain good precepts from beings who are not to be harmed. This would be a flaw, so it is not the case.
content.pt:
The seven virtues of moral discipline are: not killing, not stealing, not lying, not slandering, not consuming intoxicants, not engaging in sexual misconduct, and not taking life.

Question: Can these virtues of moral discipline be attained by non-sentient beings?

Answer: Yes, but they must be conditioned by sentient beings. These virtues of moral discipline are of three kinds: precepts, meditation, and samadhi.

Question: Why are the precepts of the path to liberation not mentioned?

Answer: The precepts of the path to liberation are included in the latter two, so they are not mentioned separately. Some scholars say there is also the precept of extinction, which is attained when one leaves the desire's realm. It is called “extinction” because it breaks the evil of breaking precepts, but in reality, all precepts are included in the three categories.

Question: Do heretics attain this precept of morality?

Answer: Yes, because they also abandon all evils with a deep mente. The precept-giver instructs: “From today onward, you should not commit the sins of killing, etc.”

Question: Do beings of other paths obtain these precepts and disciplinary rules?

Answer: The sutras state that even dragons can receive the precepts for one day. Therefore, it should be possible.

Question: Some say that those who cannot be men have no precepts or disciplinary rules. How is this to be understood?

Answer: These precepts and disciplinary rules arise from the mente. Those who cannot be men also have a good mente. Why should they not obtain them?

Question: Why are they not permitted to become monks?

Answer: Because such people have deep-rooted defilements and find it difficult to attain the path.

Moreover, such people are neither monks nor nuns, so they are not permitted. Additionally, in that order, others are also prohibited, such as those with eye defects, yet such people can still receive this virtuous precepts.

Question: In the Vinaya, those who commit perverse offense, dwell as thieves, or defile nuns are not permitted to become monks. Do such people also possess virtuous precepts?

Answer: If such a person is a layperson or has obtained good precepts, they are not prohibited from practicing virtuous deeds such as generosity and compassion. If there are those in the world who have precepts, what fault is there in that? It is merely because such a person is defiled by evil karma and obstructed from the noble path, hence they are not permitted to ordain.

Question: Do good precepts obtained from beings that may be killed apply to all beings?

Answer: They apply to all beings. If not, then the precepts would be divided. If divided, they would not be complete.

Furthermore, these precepts could be increased or decreased, similar to the teachings of the Niyana sect, which states that within a hundred yojanas one should not kill living beings, etc. Such flaws exist, therefore the precepts have no distinctions. If someone says, “I have abandoned killing toward this person, but this person has not abandoned it,” then this person has not obtained this precept. Some scholars say that if one distinguishes between the merits of giving, practicing compassion, etc., and the precepts, the precepts can also be distinguished. For example, by keeping one precept, one obtains the merit of the precept. Similarly, by keeping one precept for one being, one obtains the precepts.

Question: Are there two kinds of precepts and precepts—one for a lifetime and one for a day and night? The one for a lifetime refers to monks and laypeople. The one for a day and night refers to taking the eight precepts. How is this for a day and night?

Answer: This is not fixed. It may be one day and one night, or just one day, or just one night, or half a day, or half a night. It is obtained according to one's ability to receive it for 118 hours. Those who have renounced the world should only vow for the duration of their lives. If one says, “I will only vow for one month or two months, or just one year,” this is not called obtaining the monastic precepts. The five precepts are the same.

Answer: It is not lost, but it is defiled by unwholesome actions.

Answer: They are obtained from beings of the three past lives. Just as one gains merit by offering to those one respected in the past, so too with the precepts and discipline. Therefore, all Buddhas share the same precepts, and the precepts are immeasurable. Similarly, one person can gain precepts from all beings, and since this is attained moment by moment, there are innumerable kinds.

Answer: Some receive the one-day precepts as the first discipline, then on the same day receive the layperson’s precepts as the second discipline, then on the same day ordain as a novice monk as the third discipline, then on the same day receive the full precepts as the fourth discipline, then on the same day attain samadhi as the fifth discipline, then on the same day attain the formless realm as the sixth discipline, and then on the same day attain the extinction of defilements as the seventh discipline. Depending on where one attains the fruit of the path, one further attains the discipline, but the original discipline is not lost; only the superior one is named. In this way, merit and virtue increase. With this precept and discipline, all beings constantly attain it in every moment, hence it is said that the precepts of one day surpass the four great treasures by more than sixteen parts. The discipline of meditation and the discipline of nirvana follow the mente, while the discipline of precepts does not follow the mente.

Answer: They are always present. This person has attained the truth and does not commit evil deeds, which contradicts breaking precepts. They always refrain from evil and their virtuous mente grows stronger, so they should always be present.

Question: If there are no broken precepts in meditation or the formless realm, what contradicts them to be called virtuous precepts?

Answer: The Dharma should be like this. All sages and nobles attain virtuous precepts. If one were to say that precepts exist because they are contrary to breaking precepts, then one should only obtain good precepts from beings who are not to be harmed. This would be a flaw, so it is not the case.

segments.label: 113 八戒齋品 (On the Eight Precepts | Preceitos)

content.zh:
八戒齋名優婆娑。優婆娑，秦言善宿，是人善心離破戒宿，故名善
宿。
問曰：何故正說離八事耶？

答曰：此八是門，由此八法離一切惡，
是中四是實惡，飲酒是眾惡門，餘三是放逸因緣。是人離五種惡是
福因緣，離餘三種是道因緣。白衣多善法劣弱，但能起道因緣故，
以此八法成就五乘。
問曰：是八分齋但應具受、為得分受？

答曰：隨力能持。有人言，
此法但齋一日一夜。是事不然，隨受多少戒，或可半日乃至一月，
有何咎耶？有人言，要從他受。是亦不定，若無人時，但心念口言
我持八戒。是戒五種清淨，一行十善道、二前後諸善、三不為惡心
所惱、四以憶念守護、五回向涅槃。能如是齋，則四大寶藏不及其
一分，天王福報亦所不及。帝釋說偈，佛訶之：若漏盡人應說此
偈。偈言：
「六齋神足月， 奉行於八戒，
此人獲福德， 則為與我等。」
受此齋法應泥洹果，故漏盡人應說此偈。受齋法中，繫縛桎梏皆應
放捨，亦斷一切不善因緣，是名清淨。
問曰：轉輪聖王好受齋法，誰教之者？

答曰：大德天神曾見佛者教
之令受。
content.en:
The Eight Precepts are called the Upasaka Precepts. Upasaka means “good host” in Chinese, referring to one whose good mind is free from the past karma of breaking precepts, hence the name “good host.”

Question: Why is it specifically said to avoid the eight things?

Answer: These eight are the gates. Through these eight dharmas, one abandons all evil. Among these, four are actual evils, drinking alcohol is the gate to all evils, and the remaining three are causes of indulgence. Those who abandon the five kinds of evil are causes of merit, and those who abandon the remaining three are causes of the path. Laypeople have many good dharmas but are weak. They can only cause the causes of the path. Therefore, through these eight dharmas, the five vehicles are accomplished.

Question: Should these eight-part fasts be fully received to be considered received?

Answer: They should be observed according to one's ability. Some say that this practice is only for one day and one night. This is not correct. Depending on how many precepts one receives, one may observe for half a day or even a month. What fault is there in that? Some say that one must receive them from another. This is also not fixed. If there is no one present, one may simply think in one's mind and say aloud, “I observe the eight precepts.” These precepts have five kinds of purity: first, practicing the Ten Virtues; second, all good deeds before and after; third, not being troubled by evil thoughts; fourth, protecting oneself with mindfulness; fifth, directing one's efforts toward Nirvana. Those who observe this fast in this way will not be surpassed even by a fraction of the Four Great Treasures, and the blessings of the Heavenly Kings will not reach them. Indra recited a verse, and the Buddha rebuked him: “Only those who have eradicated all defilements should recite this verse.” The verse says: “The six fasting days are like the moon, observing the eight precepts, this person gains merit, and is equal to me.” Those who receive this fasting method should attain Nirvana, therefore those who have extinguished all defilements should recite this verse. In the fasting method, all bonds and shackles should be released, and all unwholesome causes should be severed; this is called purity.

Question: The Wheel-Turning Holy King enjoys receiving the fasting method. Who taught him?

Answer: The great virtuous deity who had seen the Buddha taught him to receive it.

segments.label: 114 八種語品 (The eight kinds of speech | Sobre The eight kinds of speech)

content.zh:
八種語，四種不淨、四種淨。四不淨者，若人見言不見、不見言
見、不見謂見問言不見、見謂不見問則言見，如是事倒心倒，故名
不淨。四種淨者，若見言見、不見言不見、見謂不見問言不見、不
見謂見問則言見，事實心實，故名曰淨。聞覺知亦如是。
問曰：見聞覺知有何差別？

答曰：有三種信，見名現在信，聞名信
賢聖語，知名比知，覺名分別。三種信慧，此三種慧或皆是實、或
皆顛倒，上人不起不淨但起淨語，是故下人所用則名不淨，上人所
用故名為淨。有人言，是義中諸正智人皆名為上，不但得道，故凡
夫人亦有淨語。
content.en:
The four impurities, and the four purities. The four impurities are: if a person sees but says he does not see, does not see but says he sees, does not see but says he sees when asked, or sees but says he does not see when asked, then his mind is inverted, and this is called impurity. The four purities are: if a person sees and says he sees, does not see and says he does not see, does not see but says he sees when asked, or sees but says he does not see when asked, then the facts and his mind are both true, and this is called purity. Hearing, perceiving, and knowing are the same.

Question: What is the difference between seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing?

Answer: There are three kinds of faith: seeing is called present faith, hearing is called faith in the words of the wise, knowing is called comparative knowledge, and perceiving is called discrimination. There are three kinds of discernment: these three kinds of discernment may all be true or all be inverted. Those of high attainment do not cause impure speech but only to pure speech. Therefore, when used by those of low attainment, it is called impure, and when used by those of high attainment, it is called pure. Some say that in this meaning, all those with right discernment are called superior beings, not just those who have attained the Way, so even ordinary people have pure speech.
content.pt:

The four impurities are: if a person sees but says he does not see, does not see but says he sees, does not see but says he sees when asked, or sees but says he does not see when asked, then his mente is inverted, and this is called impurity. The four purities are: if a person sees and says he sees, does not see and says he does not see, does not see but says he sees when asked, or sees but says he does not see when asked, then the facts and his mente are both true, and this is called purity. segments.label: 115 九業品 (The nine kinds of karma | Karma)

content.zh:
九種業，欲界繫業三種，作、無作、非作非無作，色界繫業亦如
是，無色界二種及無漏業。身口所造業名作，因作所集罪福常隨。
是心不相應法名為無作。亦有無作但從心生。非作非無作者即是
意，意即是思，思名為業。是故若意求後身，此亦名意業亦名為
思，思念後身故名為業。
問曰：若爾，則無無漏思。

答曰：若以此為思，則無無漏也。
問曰：是無作雖從身生，當有多少差別不？

答曰：若一切身分皆起
作業，因此則集多無作得大果報。
問曰：是無作在何處？

答曰：業道體定集，無作或有或無，餘則待
心，若強心則有、軟心則無。又此無作亦從願生，若人發願：我要
當布施，若起塔寺。是人定得無作。
問曰：是無作幾時得幾時失？

答曰：隨所作事在。若起園林塔寺等
施，隨施物不壞，爾時常隨。又隨心不息，如人發心：我應常作此
事，若會同若衣施。如是等事在心不息，爾時常得。又隨命未盡，
如人受出家戒，爾時常得。
問曰：有人言，但欲界中從作生無作，色界中無。是事云何？答
曰：應在二界。

所以者何？色界諸天亦應能說法、禮佛及僧。如是
人等，云何不從作業生無作耶？又有人言，隱沒無記無無作。是事
不然，隱沒無記是重煩惱，是煩惱集則名為使。但不隱沒無記無無
作。

所以者何？是心下軟不能起集，如華能熏麻非草木等。有人
言，過梵世上無有能起作業心。

所以者何？覺觀能起口業，彼無覺
觀，但用梵世心能起口業。是事不然，眾生隨業受身，若上地生不
應用梵世中報，故知以自地心能起口業。又汝說彼無覺觀，後當說
有。
問曰：聖人斷結未盡，能起作業不？

答曰：聖人不能起實罪業。
問曰：狗等眾生音聲是口業不？

答曰：雖無言辭差別，從心起故亦
名為業。又若現相、若號令、若簫竹等音皆名口業。是身口業要由
意識能起，非餘識也。是故人有自見身業、自聞口業，以意識所起
業相續不斷故自見聞。
content.en:
The nine kinds of karma are the three kinds of karma bound to the desire's realm: action, non-action, and neither action nor non-action. The karma bound to the form realm is the same, and the karma bound to the formless realm has two kinds, as well as the karma of the formless realm. Karma created by the body and mouth is called “action.” The sins and merits accumulated through action constantly follow one. The mind is not a corresponding dharma, so it is called “non-action.” There is also non-action that arises solely from the mind. Neither action nor non-action is the mind. The mind is thought, and thought is called karma. Therefore, if the mind seeks a future life, this is also called “mental karma” and “thought.” Since it thinks of a future life, it is called karma.

Question: If that is the case, then there is no untainted thought.

Answer: If this is considered thought, then there would be no untainted thought.

Question: Is there any difference in the amount of non-volitional action, even though it arises from the body?

Answer: If all bodily parts engage in action, then many non-volitional actions arise, leading to a great karmic result.

Question: Where does non-volitional action reside?

Answer: The nature of the karmic path is fixed and accumulates; non-volitional action may or may not exist. The rest depends on the mind: if the mind is strong, it exists; if the mind is weak, it does not exist.

Furthermore, this non-volitional action also arises from vows. If a person vows, “I will make offerings or build a stupa,” that person will certainly attain non-volitional action.

Question: When is non-volitional action attained and when is it lost?

Answer: It depends on the action performed. If one builds a garden, stupa, or makes offerings, as long as the object of offering remains intact, it is always present. Additionally, it persists as long as the mind continues. For example, if a person vows, “I should always perform this action, such as making offerings when clothes are worn,” Such matters, as long as they remain in the mind, are always attained.

Furthermore, they persist as long as life continues, like a person who has taken the monastic vows.

Question: Some say that in the desire's realm, the unconditioned arises from conditioned causes, but in the form realm, it does not. How is this to be understood?

Answer: It should be in both realms. Why? Because the gods of the form realm should also be able to teach the Dharma, pay respects to the Buddha, and honor the Sangha. How can such beings not arise from action into non-action? Some say that latent, indeterminate, and non-action do not arise. This is incorrect. Latent, indeterminate, and non-action are heavy defilements. When defilements accumulate, they are called “drunska.” Only latent, indeterminate, and non-action do not arise. Why? Because the mind is too weak to cause accumulation, like flowers that can perfume hemp but not trees or grass. Some say that beyond the Brahma realm, there is no mind capable of giving rise to karma. Why is this so? Perception and reflection cause verbal karma, but there is no perception or reflection there. Only the mind of the Brahma realm can cause verbal karma. This is not the case. Sentient beings receive bodies according to their karma. If they are reborn in a higher realm, they should not receive the fruit of their karma in the Brahma realm. Therefore, it is known that the mind of one’s own realm can cause verbal karma.

Furthermore, you say that there is no perception or reflection there, but later you will say that there is.

Question: Can a sage who has not completely severed the knots of defilement perform karmic actions?

Answer: A sage cannot perform actual sinful actions.

Question: Are the sounds made by dogs and other beings considered verbal actions?

Answer: Although they lack verbal distinctions, they arise from the mind and are therefore also called actions.

Furthermore, sounds such as displaying signs, issuing commands, or playing flutes are all called verbal actions. Verbal actions of the body and speech are primarily generated by consciousness and not by other consciousnesses. Therefore, people have the karma of seeing their own body and hearing their own voice, because the consciousness continuously gives rise to karma.
